# vegansexplore-com — CLAUDE Working Rules

## Stack
Static HTML site. No build pipeline. Vercel serves the repo root directly
(`outputDirectory: "."`). All pages are `.html` files. Styling is inline CSS
in `<style>` blocks. No separate CSS files. No framework.

## The template gate (Sean, 2026-11-02): never build from a blank file

"It's like you just made something up. Not following any templates, not using any previous examples... We need a system. That's why
we have systems, so we don't waste time and usage." Canon `canon-template-gate` (always loaded), error registry
`UI-BUILT-FROM-BLANK-NOT-TEMPLATE`. Before writing any new page or view, and before redoing one:

1. **Name its parent** from this map and copy that file; change only the content.
   | Building | Copy from |
   |---|---|
   | A Guide, a sampler, anything a Guide walks people through | `guides/vegan-dairy-guide.html` (`docs/guides/BUILD-A-GUIDE.md`); the whole cast: `passport.html?guide=welcome` |
   | A walkthrough, pitch, mock or concept page | `/partners` with `/public/ve-guided.js` |
   | A working tool, queue or console | `admin/depot/social.html` and the Depot pages |
   | A sign-up or a form of more than one section | `claim.html` (`?step=`) |
   | A listing or profile | `directory/listing.html` |
   | A browse page with a banner | `/public/ve-city-banner.js`, as the Directory and Events use it |
   | A search box or a results page | `/public/ve-search.js` and `search.html` (universal search, below) |
   | An email | `email-send`, as `ve-nurture` and `ve-people-outreach` call it |
   | A city restaurant carousel for social | Canva `DAHaJ8TQI0I` "5 Vegan Restaurants to Try in Philadelphia" in Vegans Explore > Directory (canon `canon-ve-city-carousel`) |
2. **Nothing fits?** Stop and bring Sean a recommendation (which parent, or a new template) before building.
3. **Before it ships**, screenshot the new page beside its parent at 1440 and 390 px. If they do not read as the same family, it does
   not ship. A new template joins this table and the canon.

First case: `/guides/taste` had been written from a blank file twice; on 2026-11-02 it was rebuilt on the Welcome Guide (see Earn your
Passport, part 3).

## The Overview is a tour, then the Guide steps back (LOCKED by Sean 2026-11-07, canon `canon-ve-guide-tour-standard`)

"Having the guides take them through all of the different pages and tabs... it's a little disorienting." Supersedes the Start here card and
the Overview standard below (their beats live inside the tour). The Overview is a full tour of the Guide: Play runs a moving slideshow synced
to the Guide's voice (welcome, I'm <Guide>; you've reached the <name> Guide and the transformation; one beat per section, each on a picture of
that tab with the part named lit up; where to start; I'm here, I take what I can't answer to our team, hide me, tap me on any page and I'll
summarize it), chapter dots and Skip the tour, about 90 seconds. Each section's beat is its own recorded chapter: back to back the tour, alone
that page's **Summarize this page**. On every other page the Guide starts hidden as **Ask <Guide>**; tapping opens a chat with suggestions on
top (Summarize this page first and free, Where do I start?, What can I do here?, real saved questions), then the ask box and Ask a person.
Visitors see the whole tour. The summary keeps a voice on every page (`ve-audio-accessibility`). The Dairy Guide stays as it is until Sean says
otherwise. Pilot: the Vegan Restaurant Guide (script `docs/proposals/restaurant-guide-tour-script.md`, waiting on Sean), then the Events Guide.
How to build it: `docs/guides/BUILD-A-GUIDE.md`.
**v2 (Sean, 2026-11-07)**: V narrates the Depot and BrandDesk ("she's the face of that part of it"); the member Guides keep their own characters. One tour,
three uses: the live tour, each chapter as its page's summary, and the same slides and voice rendered as a video for emails (a still with a play button
linking to a watch page through a tracked /go/ link), social and client calls. Animating the Guide on the Overview tours, like the Dairy Guide, comes after
every tour is locked, not before. Build order: the Depot home and its tour (prototype, script `docs/proposals/depot-tour-script.md`, waiting on Sean;
mock `/mocks/depot/`), the BrandDesk Overview tour (client version first), its video, then the Restaurant Guide. One shared tour player for all of them,
built on BrandDesk's existing V tours (`lib/branddeskTours.ts` in lesaruss-hq).
**v3 (Sean, 2026-11-07, decided first on the Nonprofit Guide): the Overview tour is a video, not a live slideshow.** It plays on the Overview, goes on our
YouTube, is downloadable, and is cut into clips for social and the podcast. Pipeline: 1. script approved; 2. each chapter recorded in the roster-profile voice and
checked with stt (unchanged); 3. a **lookbook** of every shot per chapter for Sean to approve before any animation or credits; 4. animation, the Guide on camera
with lip sync (the Dairy Guide standard); 5. the edit, chapters as video chapters, and Summarize this page still plays that chapter. The live slideshow player is
dropped. The Depot's 13 chapters are already recorded (step 2 done).
**Depot > Guides > Guides and tours** (`/admin/depot/guides`, built 2026-11-07; Sean: "it should be something that lives within the guide section we're
creating in the depot, where we can see everything, all the assets, all the recordings"): every tour video's back end, the lookbook living here instead of an
artifact. `#list`; `#t/<slug>/lookbook` (each chapter's line and recording, then its shots: **On camera** with the exact seconds of her words, **Page capture**,
**Illustration** (an idea until approved, then drawn), each **Approve** or **Redo** with a note, or Undo); `#t/<slug>/script` (each recording, its version and the
word-for-word check); `#t/<slug>/video` (the edit, once made). Tables `ve_video_tours`, `ve_video_chapters`, `ve_video_shots` (migration
`20261107_tour_backend.sql`; named ve_video_* because `ve_tours` is the old Tours feature), through `ve-depot` `tours`, `tour`, `shot_decide`, `chapter_approve`.
**On camera is three short moments** (Sean: "first 2.5 seconds, maybe in the middle, and then at the end"): lip sync needs about 3 s, so each is cut at a natural
pause and held to 3 s with the mouth closed. The rest is B-roll of the real pages plus a few illustrations. **The Depot tour** is the first: 13 chapters (1:56), 19
shots; V on camera at chapter 1 (0 to 2.4 s), 9 (0 to 2.5 s) and 13 (6.9 to 9.6 s), from her existing closed-mouth start frames
(`geekfon-media/artists/v/business-tour/join-1-v2.jpg`, `join-5-v2.jpg`, `start-4-v2.jpg`, no new credits); 12 real Depot captures at 1920 x 1080 in
`vegan-media/media/tours/depot/`; two illustration ideas (chapters 7 and 9). Next: Sean approves the lookbook, then the three moments are lip-synced and the video
is edited. The Nonprofit Guide (Dani) is the next tour to load here.
**The lookbook format (LOCKED by Sean 2026-11-07, "let's lock it"; canon `canon-ve-guide-tour-standard` v4 `lookbook_format_v4`; migration
`20261107_lookbook_frames.sql`)**: modelled on the Nonprofit Guide's lookbook artifact, with a white player, Approve and Redo on every card, and readiness
kept apart from the decision. The Lookbook tab (`lookbook()`, `frameCard()` in `admin/depot/guides.html`) is a white player (the frame, its words and time,
Play the tour through the chapter recordings back to back, Back / Next, a tappable progress bar, numbered frame buttons colored by decision), a legend, then
one card per frame in play order (01 to N): picture, global time, readiness (`ve_video_shots.readiness`: Ready, Recapture, Mock, B-roll), decision
(Waiting for you, Approved, Redo), section, the quoted words (`line`), On screen, an orange note when the script names something not built (`flag`), Play
from here, Approve / Redo / Undo (a Redo note can be spoken with the site mic). An illustration is B-roll inside the frame whose window it shares, with its
own decision. `audio_from` / `audio_to` are each frame's window in its chapter; a split inside a chapter is by sentence (approximate) unless stt word
timings are taken. The Depot tour is 17 frames (19 decisions); its orange notes: Logos as its own tool, See every page, Ask V.

## Every Guide opens the same way, and businesses earn the word Vegan (Sean, 2026-11-06)

Canon `canon-ve-guide-overview-standard`: "we need to address the elephant in the room, let them know they're in the right place, give them an
idea of what they can expect, and then clearly lay out the transformation... let them know how to use this guide... educate them... inspire them...
remove any obstacle... feel free to ask our guide... and if I can't answer your questions, we'll escalate it to one of our team members." Every
Guide's Overview, before any doing, in order: the elephant in the room, you're in the right place (who it is for), why it exists, what to expect,
the transformation and what finishing means (a short checklist), how to use the Guide, inspire and remove obstacles, then the Guide in first person:
ask me, and our team if I can't answer. Promise only what exists (Talk to <Guide>). First: the Pre-Vegan Business Guide
(`docs/proposals/pre-vegan-business-guide-overview.md`, waiting on Sean), then each Guide with Sean reading its script.

Canon `canon-ve-pre-vegan-meaning`: Pre-Vegans is a dignified pathway for people who are not Vegan yet, met with education and compassion; a title
for now ("I'm Pre-Vegan, working toward it"). We hold the word Vegan sacred: **a business that is not Vegan offers plant-based (Pre-Vegan) options,
never "Vegan options", in our own copy**; it earns the word Vegan. We use the right words without lecturing about the rule. A **tasting night** is
invited, valued members tasting a business's dishes and sending honest, constructive feedback, anonymous to the business through our app (our team
knows who said what); it ties into certification and stays Coming until one has run. Not yet changed without Sean: the Directory's "Vegan options"
label, the Restaurant Guide and the certification copy.

**Four badges for businesses (LOCKED by Sean 2026-11-06, "lock it"; canon `canon-ve-business-badges`; migration
`20261106_business_badges_canon.sql`).** **100% Vegan** (everything Vegan, run for the animals), **100% Plant-based** (everything plant-based,
the owner does not claim the Vegan motivation; respected, never a lower badge), **Pre-Vegan Certified** (named items we checked to Standard
V1.2; about the items, not the whole business; the badge opens the boxes they passed), **Pre-Vegan** (any business with plant-based options).
The owner's own intake answers set 100% Vegan or 100% Plant-based; we never judge it for them, they see the badge before it shows and can
change their answers, and our team checks before 100% Vegan shows. It is peace of mind for customers and protection for the owner, never a
penalty; a plant-based place that later adds meat broke no promise. 100% Vegan businesses get more from us (first in features and on the
podcast, the most help staying open). Our copy never names a real business or owner as an example of either badge. **Not built**: the badges
on listings, the Directory's Vegan options label (a later step).

**The badge intake, built 2026-11-06** (Sean: "approved", with Logan's defaults; migration `20261106_business_badge_intake.sql`, run through the one-time
`ve-once-badge-intake`, now the 410 stub; handoff `docs/handoff/2026-11-06-ve-pre-vegan-business-guide-badge-intake-built.md`). Four shared questions
replace "How Vegan is what you run?" (`vegan_level`) in the Restaurant, Events and Pre-Vegan Business intakes: `biz_all_plant` (Is everything you sell
plant-based?), `biz_word` (Vegan. We run it for the animals. / Plant-based), `biz_beyond` (beyond the plate: all, mostly, not yet), `biz_help`. `r_vegan`
and `e_vegan` are Question 1 now. **Questions can be skipped**: `ve_survey_questions.show_if {q, in}`, `ve_survey_states` (shown, skipped, waiting); a
skipped question is never required and pays its points as if answered, so every path pays the full total (Restaurant and Events 250, 20 a question;
Pre-Vegan Business 100, 10/5/5/5). `ve-guide-survey.js` skips them, counts only shown ones and shows **Your badge** (Change my answers, Continue) when the
answers set or change it. **The badge** is `ve_business_badges` (one row a member, kept by a trigger on `ve_member_shared_answers`; history
`ve_business_badge_events`): 100% Vegan waits for the team (`checking`, shows 100% Plant-based meanwhile); Vegan + Mostly or Not yet shows 100%
Plant-based (`follow_up`); Plant-based and Pre-Vegan show at once; leaving 100% Vegan clears its approval. **Depot > Business badges**
(`/admin/depot/badges`, Directory; edge function `ve-badges`): Waiting for a check, Team follows up, Showing, All; Approve 100% Vegan, We will follow up
first (note), Save note only (`ve_business_badge_decide`). Event sponsors' Compare scores the new answers. Proven 2026-11-06 in a rolled-back transaction
and at 1440 and 390 px against mocked answers. **Not built**: the badge on listings and cards, an email when approved, an Inbox row for a new claim.

## Nav and Footer — MANDATORY (LOCKED 2026-05-18)

Every HTML page on this site MUST include both shared component scripts.
No exceptions. No hardcoded nav or footer markup in page files.

### Required script tags

```html
<!-- Top of <body>, before any page content -->
<script src="/public/nav.js"></script>

<!-- Bottom of <body>, just before </body> -->
<script src="/public/footer.js"></script>
```

### Rules

- `nav.js` injects the sticky top nav with Guides dropdown, Communities
  dropdown, Directory, Passport links, and "Get Passport - $11" CTA.
  It also injects its own CSS. Place the script tag as the first element
  inside `<body>` (or inside the `<div class="page-frame">` wrapper if
  the page uses one).

- `footer.js` injects the dark footer with wordmark, nav links
  (ABOUT, PARTNER WITH US, POLICIES, CONTACT), social icons, and
  copyright. It also injects its own CSS. Place the script tag
  immediately before `</body>`.

- NEVER write `<nav class="ve-nav">` or `<footer class="ve-footer">`
  directly in a page file. All nav/footer changes go in the script files.

- To update nav or footer site-wide: edit `/public/nav.js` or
  `/public/footer.js` only. One edit propagates to all pages instantly.

### Exceptions (Sean, 2026-09-27)

These pages load neither nav.js nor footer.js, on purpose. Anything not on
this list follows the rule above. A new exception goes on this list first.

- **Redirect stubs**, pages whose only job is to send the visitor elsewhere
  (a meta refresh or `location.replace`, or a `vercel.json` redirect that
  catches the URL before the file is served): `partner.html` (`/partner` goes to
  `/partners`), `tour.html` (`/tour` starts the tour on the dashboard),
  `guides/ve-discuss.html`, `onboarding.html`, `apply.html` (`/apply` goes to `/claim?add=1`, Join the Directory), `welcome.html` (`/welcome` goes to
  `/passport`, the Welcome Guide, since 2026-11-08).
- **Partner pitch decks**, standalone sales documents with their own footer,
  some marked Confidential: `partners/community-partner.html` and everything
  in `partners/pitches/`. The member nav and its Passport CTA do not belong
  on them.
- **Full-screen app shell**: `app/index.html` (the body does not scroll, so a
  footer would never be seen).
- **Ad creatives**, HTML5 ads that load inside an ad slot's frame, not as pages:
  everything in `ads/` (Sean, 2026-10-04).
- **The podcast frame**, a render target for the show's pictures, not a page: `business/podcast-frame.html` (`?kind=episode|youtube|
  story|carousel`, from the podcast's brand kit; 2026-10-31).
- **Depot > Outreach**, `admin/depot/outreach.html`, removed 2026-11-08: a redirect stub to BrandDesk Outreach campaigns.
- **The offline page**, `offline.html`, shown by the service worker (`/sw.js`) when there is no connection, so it cannot count on
  nav.js or the footer loading; it is self-contained (2026-11-07, playbook `ve-mobile-app`).
- **BrandDesk client websites** (the frame), the client's own site, not a Vegans Explore page: `business/site.html`
  (`/business/sample/site`, Green Leaf Kitchen's; every real client's site, served by `branddesk-sites/`). It carries only a small "Managed by Vegans Explore BrandDesk" line (Sean, 2026-10-31).

Admin tools live in The Depot (`/admin/depot/*`) and do load both scripts. Its Go to menu (`TABS` in `public/depot-tabs.js`) was
trimmed and grouped on 2026-10-27 (Sean: "way too many things in there"): Directory (Directory review, Business outreach, Claims,
Events, Brand campaigns), Content (Inbox, Sources, Cookbook, Content index, Library), People (Community Managers, Ambassadors, Founding Members, Profiles, Bounties, Dinner guests, Links, Invites),
Site (Onboarding, Preview journeys, Dashboard checklist, Services). Logos, Pulse, Pulse Cities, Passport Partners, Tours, Passport

.ve-footer{display:none}`). The old standalone `/admin/news-review`,
`/admin/pulse-city-tags`, `/admin/opportunity-applications` and
`/admin/partner-applications` pages were retired on 2026-09-27 and redirect
to Depot > Inbox, Depot > Pulse Cities, `/dashboard/applications` and
`/dashboard/partners`. Depot > News Desk and Depot > City News were merged into
Depot > Inbox and Depot > Sources on 2026-09-28; their old URLs redirect to the Inbox.

### Why this rule exists

Before 2026-05-18 the site had 24 HTML pages with 5 different footer
structures and 3 pages missing nav entirely. A batch fix standardized all
of them. This rule prevents that drift from recurring.

### New page template

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Page Title — Vegans Explore</title>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Montserrat:wght@400;600;700;800;900&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  <style>
    /* page-specific styles here */
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="page-frame">

  <script src="/public/nav.js"></script>

  <!-- page content here -->

  <script src="/public/footer.js"></script>
  </div>
</body>
</html>
```

## Summary two-row cap (LOCKED 2026-09-14)

Every card summary / excerpt / blurb on a member-facing surface is capped at
two rows. Sean set this rule on 2026-09-13 after a Pulse entry rendered four
rows on the live site. Summaries come from Supabase (`ve_pulse_content.summary`,
`ve_community_news.summary`, `opportunities.description`,
`store_products.description`, `campaigns.summary`, `ve_board_posts.body`) and
are unbounded in length,
so the cap has to live in CSS, not in the copy.

Any class that renders one of those fields must carry:

```css
display:-webkit-box;-webkit-line-clamp:2;-webkit-box-orient:vertical;overflow:hidden;
```

Classes currently under the rule:

- `.pulse-card-excerpt` — `/pulse.html`
- `.news-excerpt` — the city hub page, `/communities/hub.html` (shared by
  `hub-news.js`, `hub-community.js` opportunity and reward cards)
- `.camp-card-desc` — `/dashboard/campaigns.html`
- `.camp-tile-desc` — `/campaigns/index.html`
- `.dash-tile-desc` — `/dashboard/center-console.html`
- `.vep-intro` — Daily Pulse topic cards, `/public/ve-pulse-topics.js` (dashboard
  Pulse tab and preview, city hubs), and `.post-body` on `/board.html`. The Daily
  Pulse became discussion topics on the Community Board on 2026-10-04; the topic
  intro (`ve_board_posts.body`) is the summary there.
- `.pulse-link-excerpt` — the "In the Pulse" section on a listing's page (`loadInPulse`
  in `directory/listing.html`), each article's summary (`ve_pulse_content.summary`).

**Directory cards in the Pulse (Sean, 2026-11-02).** Every Pulse article carries **In this story** above **On this episode** (one section, grouped by pills: People, Media,
Places, Organizations; each card keeps its vote and opens the listing): the Directory cards of the people, restaurants, brands and groups it names (`api/pulse-article.js`, loaded from `ve_content_mentions`). A listing's page
shows **In the Pulse** with the articles that name it. Matches are built by `ve_content_mentions_build` (cron
`ve-content-mentions`, every 15 minutes, an article once a day or when it changes): a person credited on the episode (not
as its host), the listing's website or Instagram linked in the text, or its full name as whole words (one-word names only for Documentaries & Films).
Our four shows and their hosts, and a stop list of plain phrases, are left out (`c_skip`, `c_stop`). A wrong match is taken
off in **Depot > In this story** (`ve-mentions`); a removed row is never rebuilt. Not yet: the city Daily Pulse topics.

**The episode page's player and people (Sean, 2026-11-03).** Every episode we can match to its feed plays through the show page's own episode row
(`VEEpisodes.row`, docked player, Save), YouTube-video episodes included; only a moment link (`?t=<seconds>`, from the content index's search)
keeps the YouTube player, since that second is timed on the video. **On this episode** lists Guest then Host (`ve_person_credits`), then
**Discussed**: People profiles the episode's own text names, read from the same `ve_content_mentions` matches In this story uses (People
sections only, `PEOPLE_CATS` in `api/pulse-article.js`; a wrong one comes off in Depot > In this story; Discussed people are left out of the
structured-data `actor` list). As transcripts are added the matcher finds more. Klaper's missing Guest credits on two episodes were added the
same day; an episode with a guest but no Guest credit reads Discussed until it is credited (audit open, see the playbook below). The work is
tracked in the playbook `podcast-network-transcript-upload` (all four shows' transcripts; closes when every episode with audio has one).

The cap applies to the card only. Full article and detail views
(`.article-lede`, `.article-p`) are never clamped.

## Ad rail (Sean, 2026-10-04)

Three-fourths content, one-fourth ads on the right, on: the Daily Pulse (`/pulse`, every tab and post, and so the
dashboard Daily Pulse tab), the dashboard Events tab, `/events`, the Directory (`/directory` and the
dashboard Directory tab) and Media (`/media` and the dashboard Media tab, the chapter's rail like the Directory's). Not on
Communities or Tools (a Directory listing page has its own billboard).

The Directory's rail is the **chapter's** (Sean, 2026-10-26: "those banners will appear throughout the entire chapter...
Central Florida will have its own... all that's real estate that people can purchase ads on"): two 300 x 250 banners stacked,
the same two landscape slots as that city hub's billboard (`<adPrefix>-landscape-1/-2`, page `/communities/<slug>`), so one
buy runs on every page of the chapter; All cities uses `/directory`'s pair (`ve-directory-landscape-1/-2`). The rail is
`data-ad-page="chapter"` and follows the city picker (`VEAdRail.chapter(rail, slug)`). Beside it the Directory is three cards
across (two under 1280 px, one on phones), and a card's name shows whole, up to four rows, never cut with an ellipsis. The card's right side is the count over **Votes** (the word is the button) and, for super admins, **More** (a dropdown with Edit and Review, room for more; `adminBtn` in `ve-region-directory.js`; Sean, 2026-10-27).

**One ad per page** (Sean, 2026-10-27: "it's either going to be the long one or two short ones, not both"): the Pulse
(and its post pages, `api/pulse-article.js`), Events and the city hubs show one tall 300 x 600; the Directory and Media show
the chapter's two 300 x 250s; a Directory listing keeps its one 300 x 250 in the info column (Sean, 2026-09-27). A city hub's
rail is its tall slot (`data-ad-page="hub"`, `data-ad-chapter` the hub slug; the rotating Billboard is gone), at the Pulse's
width (three-fourths and one-fourth, the slot a full 300 px). Under every ad, filled or not, **Your ad here / Advertise with
Vegans Explore** links to `/business#/found`, the business page's Get found (`CTA` in the script; Sean, 2026-10-27). The rail sticks 16px under
the site's menu (`--ve-nav-h`, set by `nav.js`).

**Every slot filled** (retired 2026-10-31 for our Guides, below; Sean, 2026-10-27: "imagine Humble Cabbage wasn't one of our brands... a test campaign pre-launch... and
we can slowly systematically update the real estate later on"; migration `20261027_humble_cabbage_test_campaign.sql`). Every
slot the site draws carries a Humble Cabbage ad under its one sponsor campaign (`ad_sponsor_campaigns` `humble-cabbage`), its
characters spread across pages (never the paused "$5 to the LESARUSS Foundation" art), each page with its own tracked link
(`/go/hc-ve-events`, `hc-ve-all-cities`, `hc-ve-<city>`, besides `hc-ve-pulse`, `hc-ve-sofl`, `hc-ve-directory`), so impressions
(`ad_impressions`) and clicks read by page. A real advertiser takes a slot by replacing that slot's Humble Cabbage campaign.

**House banners on listings** (Sean, 2026-10-31: "create that for other guides and sprinkle it throughout the website... that's the
only banner on the right-hand side... remove the humble cabbage... make sure we're tracking it in ads... which member clicked it, how
many times they clicked it... follow-up communications"; migration `20261031_house_banners.sql`). A Directory listing's right column
has no billboard or Humble Cabbage any more: a **People page** shows only "Is this you?" and the **Become a creator** banner, and **every
other listing** (not a brand page, which keeps its Guide house ad) shows one animated **Guide banner** (`guideBanner` in
`directory/listing.html`, `VEPromo.guideCard` and `GUIDE_ADS` in `public/ve-promo.js`): the Airport, Dairy or Stadium & Arena Guide at
random; four scenes from the Guide's own art, a headline each, a
line and Get the <Guide> · $11; never the Guide the listing's Guide tab shows (below), so a food place's is the Airport or Stadium &
Arena Guide. A demo page shows it without counting (`preview`). **Tracked as ads**: the sponsor campaign
`ve-house-banners` (Vegans Explore) holds a campaign per banner, linked to two placements, the listing's right column
(`ve-listing-house-banner`) and the People page's (`ve-people-house-banner`), with their own `page_slug` so `ad-resolve` never counts
them; the page counts a view (the banner on screen, bots left out) and a click into `ad_impressions` through `ve_house_ad_count`, which
takes only this sponsor's campaigns. **Members by name**: each banner leaves through its own tracked link (`/go/ve-guide-airport`,
`ve-guide-dairy`, `ve-guide-stadium`, `ve-creator-banner`; initiative `ve-house-banners`, tags `house-banner` and the Guide), so
`ve-links` logs every click, `nav.js` names the signed-in member on it, and `ve_initiative_interest` keeps each member's clicks and count
for `/dashboard/leads` (filter the campaign ve-house-banners and the Guide's tag, export for follow-ups). A new Guide banner is a
`GUIDE_ADS` entry, an `ad_campaigns` row under the sponsor, its `ad_campaign_placements` row and its `/go/` link.

**Our Guides fill the rails, Humble Cabbage the second of each pair** (Sean, 2026-10-31: "we should have the majority of our ads be the
guides instead of Humble Cabbage, because that is a better front door... just make them all our guides, but just create an assortment of
them around the different places"; migration `20261031_guide_ads_retire_humble_cabbage.sql`). Every Humble Cabbage campaign and its sponsor
campaign are `paused` (kept for their history; one set back to active returns that slot). Six rail campaigns under the house sponsor
(`ve-house-banners`, ids `...0c0de5a14001` to `14006`): the Dairy, Restaurant, Stadium & Arena, Airport, Nonprofit and Creator Guides,
each the HTML5 ad `/ads/guides/guide.html?g=<guide slug>` (the listing banner's animated card: four scenes, a headline each, the Guide's
line on a tall slot, Get the <Guide> · $11; it fits any slot, and drops the line on a short or wide one) and its own `/go/` link
(`ve-guide-dairy`, `-restaurant`, `-stadium`, `-airport`, `-nonprofit`, `-creator`). Each slot carries one Guide, spread so neighbouring
slots differ and the Stadium & Arena Guide shows only in chapters with mapped venues (the plan is in the migration). `ad-resolve` counts the
impression and `ad-click` the click by slot, and `ve-links` names the member who clicked (campaign ve-house-banners on `/dashboard/leads`).
**Then, the same day** (Sean: "on the ones that have the two smaller ads together, make one of them humble cabbage... it's a little
distracting seeing both of them move at the same time... The longer ones that are the guides can stay"; migration
`20261031_pairs_humble_cabbage_second.sql`): every pair of 300 x 250s (`ve-directory-landscape-2` and each `ve-<chapter>-hub-landscape-2`)
shows that slot's own Humble Cabbage campaign again, its still image, with the Guide in slot 1; the tall slots stay Guides. Humble
Cabbage's sponsor campaign is active again; its other campaigns stay paused. A new Guide ad is a `G` entry in `guide.html`, an `ad_campaigns` row under the sponsor, its `/go/` link and the slots it takes. A real
advertiser takes a slot by linking its campaign to the placement (`ad-resolve` serves the newest active campaign linked to a slot).
**On phones the rail runs the full width** (Sean, 2026-10-31: "not full width on mobile"): at 900 px and under the slots fill the row, two
side by side where there is room and one per row on a phone, and a tall slot becomes a wide box there (`ve-ad-rail.js`).

Use `/public/ve-ad-rail.js`: wrap the content in `<div class="vear-layout"><div class="vear-main">`
and add `<aside class="vear-rail" data-ad-page="pulse|/events">`. Slots come from `ad_placements`
(page_slug + slot_id) through the `ad-resolve` function; a rail fills, and counts an impression,
only once it is on screen. A new page needs its slots added to `ad_placements` and to `PAGES` in
the script.

**Shared with seanarussell.com** (Sean, 2026-11-01, Watch: "follow that same structure, even how the audio plays"): Sean's site
loads `https://vegansexplore.com/public/ve-episodes.js` and `ve-ad-rail.js`. `VEEpisodes.mount(el, {listing, call})` takes
`call(body)` returning another site's episodes in ve-podcast's shape (sar-media `episodes`/`episode`); with it Save, Show notes
from the Pulse and Referenced books are left out. The rail takes `data-ad-brand`, `data-ad-slots` ("slot:tower:300 x 600") and
`data-ad-cta`/`data-ad-cta-label` for a page outside `PAGES`, and loads `ve-ad-creative.js` from its own origin. Keep both
scripts working when loaded from another origin.

### Ad creatives (Sean, 2026-10-04)

An ad's `creative_url` is an image or an HTML5 ad (a `.html` file in `ads/<brand>/`). Every slot
renders through `/public/ve-ad-creative.js` (`VEAdCreative.markup(ad)`), which frames an HTML5 ad
in a sandbox and passes the tracked link as `?clickTag=`; the ad opens that link itself and posts
`{veAd:'click'}` so the click counts. GeekFon artist pages do the same in
`components/AdCreative.tsx` (lesaruss/geekfon-society). Every ad link is a tracked `/go/` link.
Our guides (River, Maya, Nori and the rest) are always drawn in the GeekFon illustration style,
never photographs, in ads and everywhere else. Example: `/ads/humble-cabbage/ve-tee.html`, River
in the tee, then Shop now plays the tee, Maya and Nori in Black, the $5 donation, and Shop now.

## Full width (LOCKED 2026-10-04)

Sean, 2026-10-04: "everything full width. Just remember everything full width. We don't do fixed
width." Page containers never get a fixed `max-width` (`main{max-width:none;margin:0;padding:44px
40px 80px}`, 16px side padding on phones). Lists and cards fill the width with a grid
(`repeat(auto-fill,minmax(min(360px,100%),1fr))`) instead of one narrow column. When something
would read badly that wide (a long text column, a form), give the page the ad rail (see Ad rail:
three-fourths content, one-fourth ads) rather than narrowing it. A line of body copy can keep its
own reading width (`.sub{max-width:860px}`); the page around it cannot.

## Interface defaults (Sean, 2026-10-04)

Sean: "I feel like I keep asking for the same thing over." The full checklist is canon
`canon-sean-interface-defaults` (always loaded, every brand). Build these in on the first pass:

- One thing per view: a list, then one item on its own, with breadcrumbs back (List > Item > Sub-item).
  Edit, New and sub-items get their own view. The address bar carries the view so back works.
  No page that stacks every item, its editor and its children.
- Every row in a list has the same fields and the same single action button in the same place. Status
  is a colored tag in plain words (Live, Waiting for approval, Not live yet), never an action word.
- Full width (above). Cards four across, most urgent first. Short lists cap and scroll inside the box.
  Summaries clamp to two rows. Queues filter, sort and search. New is a button to its own view.
- **No window and no bottom bar** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "I don't like having everything wrapped together... no more universal frame,
  no more universal selector, just that apps button"). The dashboard is a plain page under a sticky top nav (no backdrop, title bar
  or traffic lights; the page scrolls), a listing opened from it is its own `/directory/<slug>` page on every screen, and HQ's
  `universal-bar.js` draws no bottom row, only the **Apps** launcher: Vegans Explore, GeekFon Society and Sean A. Russell, the same
  three everywhere (`LAUNCHER` there). Apps is in the dashboard's bar and, signed in, in `nav.js` on every page (it loads HQ's file
  on the first tap). The city hubs' section headers carry an **In this community** dropdown of the hub's sections (one-fourth,
  beside the title and line; `placePick` in `communities/hub.html`).
- Member features live in the dashboard: `/dashboard/<feature>` opens
  the page under "Dashboard / Feature". Opened on its own while signed in, the page moves into the
  dashboard; signed out, it shows a sign-in gate and none of the content, and the server refuses the
  data. Example: `/bounties` -> `/dashboard/bounties` (`openBounties` in center-console).
- Example: Depot > Bounties (`/admin/depot/bounties`): Campaigns > campaign > job, with `#new`,
  `#campaign/<id>/edit`, `#review` and `#strikes` as their own views.
- Forms with more than one section are paginated (Sean, 2026-10-09, "I've said this multiple times"; canon rule 14, error
  registry `UI-FORM-LONG-SCROLL-NOT-PAGINATED`): one step per view, the step names on top, Back / Step N of M / Next at the
  bottom, Next checks the step, the last step holds the choice and the submit, `?step=` in the address bar. Example: `/claim`.
- Dropdowns never show the browser's arrow (Sean, 2026-10-09, "always too close to the edge"; canon rule 15, error registry
  `UI-SELECT-ARROW-TOO-CLOSE-TO-EDGE`): `appearance:none`, an SVG chevron at `background-position:right 16px center`,
  `padding-right` 44px or more. Copy the `select` rule in `claim.html`.
- Buttons, tabs and inputs use a 6px corner radius, not pills (canon rule 13, Sean 2026-10-09).
- **Speak instead of typing on every field** (Sean, 2026-10-31: "make sure we have the record the dictation feature on all things
  where people are going to type in information"). `/public/ve-dictate.js`, loaded by `nav.js` on every page and by the dashboard
  itself: in any textarea or text field, a small mic floats at the field's right edge while it has focus (no page's layout changes);
  tapped, the browser's own speech recognition writes what is said at the cursor until Stop, Escape or silence (the native value setter
  and an input event, so every page's own handlers see it). Nothing is recorded by us. Left out: email, password, number, phone, web
  address and date fields, fields under 12 characters, autocomplete or inputmode for email, phone, codes or cards, a placeholder
  starting https:// or @, read-only and disabled fields, and anything marked `data-dictate="off"` (the Ambassadors, Founding Members
  and Group Partners consoles keep their own Speak buttons that way). No mic where the browser has no speech recognition (Firefox). A
  new form needs nothing: it gets the mic.

## Guided view for mocks and walkthroughs (LOCKED 2026-10-04)

Sean: "I say this every time... I don't like the scroll... put it in that view so we're
navigating through and seeing everything." Canon `canon-sean-interface-defaults` rule 0.

Any mock, demo, pitch walkthrough, illustrative report or concept page is built as the guided
view on the first pass, never a long scroll: one full-height slide at a time on a **clean white stage** (Sean, 2026-11-07:
"Why is it a green background? You should know me by now. I like the clean white background look"; `<main class="vg-stage vg-light">`,
the dark stage only for pages already built on it: /partners and the pitch decks),
Back / "N of M" / Next at the bottom, nothing to scroll on desktop (nav, stage and footer share
one screen), every slide fitting at 1440x900 and 1366x768, and on phones the slide stacks with
the controls after it. The format is the `/partners` page; the shared shell is
`/public/ve-guided.js` (see its header for the markup). Wrap the page in
`<div class="page-frame">`, put slides in `<main class="vg-stage">` as
`<section class="vg-slide" id="..." data-title="...">`, and load the script after the footer.
Different audiences branch from a `data-vg-choose` slide into `data-path` slides. Example:
`/campaign-engine`, `/campaign-engine/fieldhouse-protein/report` and `/dashboard`. Working tools and data pages
(queues, lists, forms) are not mocks and follow Interface defaults.

## Campaigns on a listing (Sean, 2026-10-04)

A brand's campaign runs on its Directory listing: `directory/listing.html` shows a campaign banner,
a Campaign tab (tasks with points, your progress, a city leaderboard, the creators), an Events tab
and a sidebar card whenever the listing carries a campaign (`l._campaign`), and Food Brands get
their Menu tab labeled Products. The demo, `/campaign-engine/fieldhouse-protein` (rewrite in
`vercel.json`), is that real page in demo mode: `?demo=<slug>` or `/campaign-engine/<slug>` loads
`/campaign-engine/<slug>/listing-demo.js` instead of the database, labels it Illustrative, turns
off votes, saves and claims, adds a member / brand view switch and a week stepper (the demo's
`campaignAt(week)` returns the campaign as it stood that week, 1 to 10, then Final), and starts a
`ve-tour.js` spotlight tour of the campaign. `/campaign-engine/fieldhouse-protein/social` shows the
campaign in our Instagram, TikTok, Community Board, Daily Pulse and member feeds. Campaign rules:
everyone starts at zero, a capped points total, joining Vegans Explore is how you enter, a grand
prize for the most points, prizes for each city's top 10, and digital rewards (coupons) at set totals. Live campaigns are not wired yet: `ve_bounty_campaigns.host_listing_id`
links a campaign to a listing, but the table has no public read, so it needs to come through the
`ve-bounties` function first.

## Business outreach, city by city (Sean, 2026-10-10)

"Let's just make sure we're not sending any emails... when I say go... let's go city by city. And not try to hit everybody
at once." Then: "see who is on the queue, approve who the emails are going to be going out to... on Monday, we're sending
it to these 60... see what the draft is... and we commit to it for like maybe 15 days before we make any drastic changes."
The goal is businesses on board for Q1 2027 through Front Row Start. Migrations `20261010_ve_outreach.sql`,
`20261010_ve_outreach_batches.sql`, `20261010_ve_outreach_sender.sql`, `20261010_ve_outreach_listing_cleanup.sql` and `20261010_ve_partner_onboarding.sql`; edge function `ve-outreach`; console **Depot > Business outreach**
(`/admin/depot/business-outreach`).

- **The console** (one thing per view): Upcoming sends (each send day is a batch: Waiting for approval, Approved, Sent) and
  the cities. A send day lists its businesses (who they are, where the email goes and where we found it, the Guides they
  are in) with Preview; a business opens its three emails exactly as they go out beside its real page (framed,
  `?preview=1`), where Sean can fix the name or email, take it out of the day or mark it Never email. **Approve this send**
  approves all three emails for that day's businesses. Plan sends proposes days: first send day and businesses per weekday
  (`ve_outreach_plan`, brands first). The first approval in a city sets its 15-day commitment
  (`ve_outreach_cities.committed_until`, shown on the city card): no big changes to the emails or the plan before then.
  An upgrade to what we offer (Sean, 2026-10-10: the free restaurant audit "still falls in the plan, it's just an upgrade
  to the offer") is not a change to the plan and can go into the emails at any time; the commitment guards the plan itself.
- **Two gates before anything sends**: the batch is approved, and the city is on (Turn on sending / Pause sending on the city
  card, `ve_outreach_cities.enabled`, every city off until Sean turns it on). `ve_outreach_due()` is what goes next: approved
  send days whose day has come, then follow-ups when due, never a suppressed address.
- **The sender** (migration `20261010_ve_outreach_sender.sql`, `ve-outreach` `tick`, cron `ve-outreach-send` every 10
  minutes): weekdays 9 AM to 5 PM Eastern only, 6 a tick (a day of 30 goes out over about an hour), within the city's
  `daily_cap` (30) and the domain's warm-up allowance (`email_warmup_allowance`). Each email goes through `email-send`
  (brand `lesaruss`: from Sean A. Russell <sean@mail.lesaruss.ai>, replies to contact@lesaruss.com, one-click unsubscribe,
  the postal address, `campaign_ref` `ve-outreach-<contact>-<step>` so nothing is sent twice) as a plain personal email with
  a small footer. The page link is the business's own tracked link (`ve_links`, `bo-<code>`, campaign `business-outreach`,
  made at its first email). Day 4 and Day 10 are set for 10 AM Eastern on a weekday. Before every tick `ve_outreach_sync()`
  reads what they did: a real click on their link or a reply (not an auto-reply) makes them Interested, a claim makes them
  Joined, an unsubscribe or block makes them Unsubscribed, a bounce Bounced, and a send day turns Sent once everyone in it
  has had their first email. Three failed sends hold a business. Heartbeat: `email_heartbeats` `ve-outreach`.
- **Send me this as a test** (a business's preview, `ve-outreach` `test`): its real email to the signed-in admin with
  [Test] in the subject and the plain page link, so the test click never counts (the ops token can only dry-run it:
  `dry_run: true` renders it and passes email-send's checks without sending). **Interested** (`#interested`, `ve-outreach`
  `interested`): who clicked, replied or claimed, what they did, and who it is routed to.
- **The emails** (`ve_outreach_templates`): three from Sean (sender `email_brands` `lesaruss`, replies to
  contact@lesaruss.com), Day 0 "We built a page for {business}", Day 4 "Your front-row seat{in_city}", Day 10 "Last note
  from me". `ve_outreach_render(contact, step)` fills them; the console and the sender both use it. `{in_city}` is " in
  South Florida" (nothing for a national brand), `{guide}` is Liz (Maya for a Dairy Guide brand), and `{guide_line}` names a
  Guide the business is in, as a brand or as a store carrying its products (`ve_outreach_guides`), with a link to it in the
  Guide (`/guides/<guide>#/listing/<slug>`). No price in the emails: the $111 is on the Partner Dashboard.
- **Contacts** (`ve_outreach_contacts`): one per public, unclaimed listing with an email, by city; national brands are
  their own row, `brands`. A click, reply or claim makes it `interested`; `trg_ve_outreach_route` stops its emails and
  routes it to the city's Community Manager, or Sean. `ve_outreach_queue` is the interest queue.
- **Find emails** (city card, `ve-outreach` `find_emails`, 20 websites a press): reads the business's own home, contact
  and about pages, server side, and takes only an email published there (mailto, plain text, Cloudflare-protected), with
  the page as `email_source`. Never guessed. Each listing is tried once (`ve_outreach_lookups`).
- Ops: `ve-outreach` also takes `LESARUSS_ADMIN_TOKEN` for overview, preview, plan and find_emails; approving, changing a
  row and the city switch need a signed-in super admin.
- **People lists: one engine for every brand** (Sean, 2026-10-10: "This should use the same engine we just created for
  Vegans Explore to do outreach. We can select people in our system and add them to the distribution"; migration
  `20261010_ve_outreach_lists.sql`). A `ve_outreach_cities` row is a list: `kind` `city` (businesses, everything above) or
  `people` (people added from HQ > People). A people list has its own `program` (its three emails are
  `ve_outreach_templates` rows with that program; business outreach is program `business-outreach`), `link_url` (where
  `{link}` goes, made into the person's tracked /go/ link at the first email), `footer_reason` ("You are getting this because
  ...") and `brand` (the HQ label), and the same switch, daily cap, send days, approval and sender. A person contact has no
  listing (`segment` `person`, `person_id`, once per list by email); `ve_outreach_render` gives them `{first_name}` and `{link}`;
  `ve_outreach_sync` marks them Joined when they become a paying LESARUSS AI member or start a 111 Day Theory journey after
  their first email. The Depot here shows cities only (`overview` defaults to kind `city`; `interested` to businesses). HQ >
  Distributions works the people lists through `ve-outreach` with the admin token and `as_member` (the owner's super admin
  member id), which is honored only for people lists; `add_people`, `templates` and `template_save` are the people-list
  actions. A people list's emails start as drafts and send only once marked ready in HQ. First list:
  `111-day-theory-founding` (program `111-day-theory`, link `https://lesaruss.com/entry/join?program=111-day-theory`).
  Before and after the migration, `ve_outreach_render` over every business contact and step rendered the same text (md5
  d0864f6f38450faca8768a7f3eb13c86, 234 emails), and the Depot's overview returned the same 9 cities, 3 emails and 2 send days.
- The June 2026 `listing_outreach` queue (the old $11 claim offer, never sent) was retired on 2026-10-10 (`skipped`, note).
- **Cleaning up the Directory from here** (Sean, 2026-10-10: "remove people from the distribution list... move them to the
  closed and move them off the main list... leave a note"). Each business's preview has **The Directory listing**: team notes
  (`listings.details.admin_notes`, `[{at, by, kind: note|closed|logo, text}]`), **No longer in business** (`listing_closed`:
  `business_status = 'CLOSED_PERMANENTLY'`, which the Directory shows only under Type > Closed, never in All, plus
  `details.closed_at`/`closed_by`/`status_before_closed`) and **Use the letter, not this logo** (`listing_logo_letter`: the
  logo is set aside in `details.logo_unverified`, the same way as the Logos rule). However a listing gets closed (here or
  the listing page's admin editor), trigger `trg_ve_outreach_listing_closed` takes it off the email list, and planning and
  Find emails skip closed businesses (migration `20261010_ve_outreach_listing_cleanup.sql`). Send days list brands first,
  then A to Z, so the order never shifts. On 2026-10-10 five businesses the Directory already marked closed came off the list
  before anything was sent, and Darbster's blurry logo was set aside for the letter (Sean).
- **Owners edit their own page** (Sean, 2026-10-10: "go ahead and build the owner page editing"). Any owner of a listing (the
  approved claim makes them `owner_member_id`), with or without a plan, gets **Edit your page** on the Partner Dashboard tab
  (`mountOwnerEditor` in `directory/listing.html`): four steps, one per view (`?tab=brand&edit=about|hours|contact|photos`),
  Back / Step N of M / Save and next: About (the one line and the description), Hours (each day in their own words, empty
  hides it, saved as `google_hours_json` {Day: text}), Contact and links (phone, website, Instagram, booking, Uber Eats,
  DoorDash, street and ZIP), Logo and photos (logo at least 400 px on the shorter side, up to 12 photos at least 1000 px,
  into `vegan-media/media/listings/<slug>/owner-*`, checked in the page and again in the function; an owner's logo replaces a
  set-aside one, `details.logo_source = 'owner'`; photos go to `gallery_urls`, which the page shows). Their name, city,
  category and how Vegan they are stay ours. Changes go live at once (`ve-claims` `owner_page`, `owner_update`,
  `owner_photo_url`, `owner_photo_done`, `owner_photo_remove`), each one a row in `ve_listing_edits` with the value it
  replaced (migration `20261010_ve_listing_edits.sql`), and the account manager (else Sean) is emailed what changed. A new
  partner's page in the Depot lists **Their changes** with **Undo** (`ve-outreach` `listing_edits`, `listing_edit_undo`, which
  refuses when the same thing was changed again since).
- **New partners: onboarding** (Sean, 2026-10-10: "go ahead and build the onboarding"; migration
  `20261010_ve_partner_onboarding.sql`). Every business that claims its page (`ve_listing_claims` paid or submitted, never a
  test) gets a `ve_partner_onboarding` row through trigger `trg_ve_partner_onboarding`: Waiting for your approval, then, when
  Sean approves the claim in Depot > Claims, Welcoming. Approval starts two things. **Automatic**: three emails from Sean after
  ve-claims' own "your page is confirmed" (`ve_onboarding_templates`, rendered by `ve_onboarding_render`): Day 2 make the page
  yours (Edit your page on the Partner Dashboard, or reply with a logo, photos and changes and we do it),
  Day 7 the first week's numbers (views and visitors from `ve_listing_events`), Day 21 what's coming in Q1 and what they want
  to be part of, plus, on Front Row Start, the date of their first charge. **Personal**: the city's Community Manager, or Sean
  when the city has none, is emailed the task (welcome them within 2 days, with their contact details and the checklist), and
  the checklist lives in **Depot > Business outreach > New partners** (`#partners`, `#partner/<listing>`): welcome them
  personally, confirm the page details, get a clear logo and photos on, ask which Q1 campaigns they want in on. A partner is
  Welcomed when it is all ticked; a welcome more than 2 days late shows Late. The same page shows their three emails (sent,
  opened, next) and the listing notes. `ve-outreach` `tick` sends the task emails (any hour) and the onboarding emails
  (weekdays 9 to 5 Eastern). While building it, `ve_listing_claims_tier_check` turned out to refuse tier `brand` (the Partner
  plan), so every Partner claim would have failed to save; widened the same day, before any claim was made.

## BrandDesk: managed marketing for Vegan businesses (LOCKED by Sean 2026-10-31, playbook `ve-front-of-house`)

**The name is BrandDesk** (Sean, 2026-10-31: "I like brand desk... it could fit for anybody, anything"; canon v7). It was called
Front of House until then; the canon and playbook slugs keep `front-of-house`. One word, B and D capitals. Trademark and domain check
before it goes on a public page (BrandDeck, a brand-management tool, is close).

Concept session with V, locked by Sean: "lock it" (canon `canon-ve-front-of-house`; migration `20261031_front_of_house_canon.sql`).
**Not built yet.** Sean: "they don't have a solid brand presence... You can't find a logo. Their website looks like it was made in 2014...
I want to create a management package for vegan businesses that's accessible... I have had somebody literally say that to me." People
judge whether food is safe by how a place looks online; businesses want marketing help, not more promotion. Restaurants are the way in.

- **The offer**: **$1,500 setup** (at once or over 3 or 6 months; the rest owed on an early cancel): the
  full audit, a logo and brand kit, Google Business Profile claimed and complete, the website on our template fed by their listing, their
  Directory page and dashboard, a starter shoot of up to 15 menu items, two weeks for what we control (Google's verification shows as
  waiting). **$500 a month**: the managed website (the template improves for every client), Google (hours, photos, posts, reviews), a
  monthly Community Manager check-in on a fixed question set, a campaign a month, live results on the business dashboard, the ad console
  with a capped allowance (worded "included the day it opens" until it is live). **Social +$500 a month** for two platforms; the shop's
  one-platform $400 stays for businesses that are not managed. 12 months, then month to month; they own their domain and content.
- **The split**: $250 to the account's Community Manager (gig work, never an amount in public copy), $250 to Vegans Explore. 10 accounts
  per Community Manager to start; a full one means hiring the next. A city opens to BrandDesk when it has a Community Manager.
- **The showroom**: Green Leaf Kitchen (`/business/sample`) gets its website on the real template, exactly what a client gets minus their
  brand; the template changes only through brand slots (fonts, colors, logo, voice, photo look), like LESARUSS.ai's variables. A
  make-it-yours switch shows it in two or three looks. `/business` gets a **Managed by us** module; the Restaurant Guide's audit links every
  Fix to it (Have us do it).
- **Photos shot like Airbnb** from a fixed shot list (outside by day and dusk, inside wide, every menu item on one surface and angle, the
  team; customers only with consent). One shoot feeds the site, Google, the delivery apps and social. New menu item: added on the dashboard,
  a shoot requested, an influencer night launches it.
- **Visits every week** from creators (perk gigs; paid macro creators as an add-on), Community Managers in house where creators are thin,
  and **member visit bounties** open to everyone: the phone's location proves the visit, a phone shooting guide on the gig, team approval
  before points, the best credited on the listing and our socials. Members pay their own meal unless the restaurant offers a perk; a comped
  visit is disclosed (FTC). Members whose shots keep being approved are scouted toward Ambassador and the Gig Board.
- **A monthly rotation** across managed businesses: influencer night, DJ night, customer appreciation, giveaways, a scavenger hunt stop, a
  community night with a coaching sheet.
- **The pitch**: a presence-gap ranking on the monthly check-ups, then a personal guided page per business (their audit, their site mocked
  on our template, the two-week plan, the price), sent from Sean through business outreach, city by city, with his approval.
- **A handshake before the ask** (LOCKED by Sean 2026-10-31, "lock it"; canon v8, migration `20261031_branddesk_handshake_canon.sql`;
  Sean: "is this too heavy of an ask for people who don't even know us?... we need a handshake before we ask them to commit to $500 a
  month"). 1. **Free**: business outreach's first email gives them their page with the top things from their free restaurant check, no
  price. 2. **$11**: the Vegan Restaurant Guide (every fix, Or have us do it; the pitch page's Not now offers it too). 3. **The BrandDesk
  pitch page** only after a sign (clicked their link, claimed, ran the free check, bought the Guide, Have us do it, Talk to someone) or for
  Sean's warm list; never a cold $500 ask. Outreach starts in the chapters with the biggest gaps and the most signs; every city stays off
  until Sean turns it on. **Both built 2026-10-31** (Sean: "then the handshakes"). **The first email** (migration
  `20261031_handshake_free_check_email.sql`): `ve_outreach_free_check(listing)` takes their latest finished audit from the last 45 days (the monthly
  check-ups), the free check's items to fix, three at most, most important first, each in the check's own words, and a link to their whole free
  check in the Vegan Restaurant Guide (`#/audit/r/<id>`, the free view for anyone); `ve_outreach_render` (the old one kept as
  `ve_outreach_render_base`, called first) fills `{free_check}`, now after the guide line in the Day 0 template. No price. A business with no recent
  check-up gets the email as it was: with the check taken back out, all 234 business emails rendered byte for byte as before; 33 of 78 first
  emails carry one. An upgrade to the offer, so it may go in during a city's 15-day commitment. **Made accurate 2026-11-01** (Sean, reviewing
  the walkthrough: "we need to 100% make sure that these things that we're saying are true... That kills our credibility"; "nothing's theirs to
  keep. They can claim it if they're a member"; "what dashboard? They haven't signed up with us"; migration `20261101_handshake_email_accuracy.sql`).
  Rootz Soul Cafe's email had said "Google has no hours" (Google marks it closed for now) and "we could not find the Instagram" (our reader
