included, end excluded, so a day is start=d end=d+1; no dates is all time), `GET /insights/<show>/overview/<episode>?start&end` (one episode),
`GET /insights/<show>/monthly` (the last 12 months, this month, the total). **The first probe said no listeners, apps, devices or places endpoint exists; that was wrong** (guessed paths
were 404). The dashboard's own paths are in its public scripts (`my.captivate.fm`, an Angular app; read them, never guess) and the same API key reads them: see **Any period, the
audience and the first days** below. The view: downloads for the period against the one before, per day (every N days past
30 days), this month, last 12 months, all time, a line by month, and every episode's downloads in the period (up to 100 s of reading, then
`partial`). Proven 2026-11-04 on real numbers (30 days to Nov 3: 258 downloads, 389 the 30 days before; the daily and per-episode numbers each
sum to 258; 144 episodes read). A new brand's show is a `PODCAST_SHOWS` row and a `PODCAST_BRANDS` entry.
**Pages from Captivate's own dashboard, uploaded by hand** (Sean, 2026-11-04: "whatever can't be pulled by API, we can upload manually with a screenshot... the
ability to upload multiple... where people are listening from, what devices... the quarterly and monthly reports"): the Podcast view ends with **From Captivate's
own dashboard** (`PodcastUploads` in `InsightsRoom.tsx`): a kind (Where people listen, Devices, Apps and players, Report or overview, Something else), the dates
it covers (the page's period by default), an optional note, and a drop box for as many PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF files as you like (25 MB each; a screenshot can be
pasted). Each file goes straight from the browser to the private bucket `podcast-reports` on a signed link, then a row in `ve_podcast_uploads` (migration
`20261104_podcast_report_uploads.sql`, RLS on, no policies) says what it is and when. They show below, by period, with Everything / kind chips, a lightbox for
pictures, Open and Remove (Remove only hides it; nothing is deleted). `branddesk-insights` actions `podcast_files`, `podcast_upload_start`, `podcast_upload_done`,
`podcast_file_remove` (super admins only; `podcast_upload_done` checks the file really is in the bucket). Proven live 2026-11-04 as Sean: a real upload to a signed link
registered, listed with a signed URL and removed; a wrong type, over 25 MB, another brand's path, a file never uploaded, bad dates and a call with no token were all
refused; the section checked at 1440 and 390 px against mocked answers (four files chosen, the wrong type flagged, three uploaded together). A 70-byte test image is
left in the bucket (Storage will not let SQL delete objects), with no row. Not yet: reading the numbers out of a screenshot into a chart, the podcast in the Analysis
write-up, first 7 and 30 day downloads per episode.

**Any period, the audience and the first days** (Sean, 2026-11-04: "if we do all time, every time you pull information... we could do a custom... use our sorters... for all of
the podcasts"; "the places are really important... both the country and the cities and provinces", to set beside Google's places and choose the next community;
`branddesk-insights` from vegansexplore-com d2fa4cb, HQ `bed59b7`, production READY, seen signed in as `vegan@lesaruss.com`; migration
`20261104_podcast_episode_firsts.sql`). **Four shows** in `PODCAST_SHOWS` (Vegans Explore, SoFlo Vegans, Vegans Who Lift, Pre-Vegans; Captivate ids from
`GET /users/<user>/shows`; its "Vegans Explore Network Exclusives" show is left out); HQ's Podcast view has a **Show** dropdown, its own **Period** (Last 7, 30, 90 days, This year,
All time, Custom dates; the Insights period box is hidden on this tab) and **Overview / Episodes / Audience / Uploads**, all in the address (`?show=&sub=&prange=&pfrom=&pto=`). **What
Captivate gives** (all probed 2026-11-04): `POST /insights/<show>/over-time` {gteUnix, lteUnix, interval} (interval must be one of 1h, 1d, 7d, 14d, 28d, 1M, 1y, null; `1d` gives
days at Eastern midnight, ms timestamps); `POST /insights/<show>/overview/range` {startTimestamp, endTimestamp} in unix seconds (a number; ms is refused) gives `byEpisode`
[{episodeId, total}] for every episode in one call; `POST /insights/<show>/range/` {start, end ISO, timezone, interval null, countryCode, types} with types `byLocation`,
`byUserAgentBrowser` (the app or player), `byUserAgentOs`, `byUserAgentDevice`; **countryCode must be sent: null gives every country (no provinces or cities), an uppercase ISO
code ("US") gives that country's provinces and cities with their parents; "us", "United States", "all" return nothing**; `POST /insights/<show>/basic` {gteUnix, lteUnix, isUnique};
`GET /insights/<show>/from-episode-publish` (each episode's first 28 days). **How it is built**: one all-time daily series per show (`over-time` 1d from the day before its
first episode, cached 3 hours, `ins:podseries:`) and every period, comparison, this month, last 12 months and the by-month line are cut from it with no new calls, so a custom range costs
nothing and "All time" starts on the first day Captivate has a download (Vegans Explore 2025-11-01, SoFlo 2020-03-03). **Audience** (`podAudience`): one range call for every
country, apps, systems and devices, then one call per country (ISO code from `Intl.DisplayNames`, `ccMap`) for its provinces and cities; places cannot be cut from daily totals, so each
period is its own cached call (3 hours). Proven: Vegans Explore all time 93 countries, 5,756 downloads, US 40 provinces and 230 cities, four countries without a code map keep only
their total; **All podcasts together** (Audience tab only) adds the four shows by name; **Download every place (CSV)** gives every country, province and city for the period.
Captivate's range total can differ a little from the daily downloads (230 against 258 on one 30-day window), and a province or city is only known where the listener's network
gives one. **First 7 and first 30 days** per episode: `ve_podcast_episode_firsts` (brand, show, episode, d7, d30, RLS on), counted once those days are over (calendar days from the
release day, Eastern), 40 episodes an Episodes visit while the page re-asks until none are left; the Episodes table sorts by any column. **View only for agent accounts**: `branddesk-insights`
refuses `podcast_upload_start`, `podcast_upload_done` and `podcast_file_remove` for `member_class` `agent` (403 `view_only`), so the standing QA login `vegan@lesaruss.com`
(already a super admin row) can read Insights and never change it; uploads are per show (`ve_podcast_uploads.show_key`, older ones stay on Vegans Explore). Captivate holds more
episodes than our table for SoFlo (111 against 59) and Vegans Who Lift (90 against 57), which may move the "all 278 transcribed" finish line. Not yet: reading numbers out of uploaded
screenshots (Sean's answer was not given; the API now covers places, apps and devices, so the uploads are for reports and anything else), a saved snapshot of the places for the community
decision (the CSV is the first step), and the one bad Vegans Who Lift failed-transcript row, which stays until Sean says delete.

## Depot > Social (Sean, 2026-11-01)

"A social media page in the VE Depot where I can see a grid of scheduled content and click in it to see the caption, tags, links,
and anything else... share analytics for all of our social feeds and make it so I can sort between channels to see scheduled and past
content." **Depot > Social** (`/admin/depot/social`, Content in the Go to menu; super admins), one thing per view: **Content**
(`#content/<scheduled|past|all>/<channel>`: channel chips with counts, Scheduled / Past / All, the period, search over captions,
hashtags and mentions; a grid four across, what goes out next first, then the newest past; each tile the picture, the channel, the
status (Scheduled, Published, Draft, Did not post), the time in Eastern, the caption in two rows and, once out, views, likes and
comments), **one post** (`#post/<id>`: the picture or episode audio, when it goes or went out, hashtags, who is tagged, every link
(a `/go/` link marked Tracked), the first comment, the network's settings, how it did, the full caption, Copy caption, Open on the
channel) and **Analytics** (`#analytics/<channel>`: a card a channel with followers, the change in the period and a line of it, posts,
views, reach and average engagement; pick one to see only its posts; every post in a table sorted by any column). Server: edge
function `ve-social` (`report` with Eastern `from` / `to`; super admin or the admin token; cached 30 minutes in `ve_analytics_cache`,
Refresh now skips it). It reads **Metricool** (`analytics_connections` `metricool`, blog 3707345: `/v2/scheduler/posts` for what is
scheduled, `/v2/analytics/posts|reels/instagram`, `/v2/analytics/posts/facebook|tiktok`, `/stats/youtube/videos`, and followers from
`/v2/analytics/timelines` with `subject=account`; Metricool gives times in Europe/Madrid, turned into UTC there) and **Captivate** for
the podcast (the show's dates are America/New_York). A post scheduled in Metricool that went out shows once, with the numbers. Checked
2026-11-01: Instagram 3,762 followers, TikTok 3,038, YouTube 584, Facebook 371. **X is not connected in Metricool** (its API says so),
though the 2026-10-31 notes said it was. Not yet: podcast downloads from Captivate, scheduling or editing from the page (it is read
only; posts are scheduled in Metricool).

**The studio** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "see what's slotted for the different brands... you propose things... the community manager goes
in... make any adjustments... or leave a note that you will then take care of... you will use your connections to push it out... If
something needs a manual thing... we know ahead of time... a calendar... track it to its metrics... between different brands...
clients"; migration `20261101_ve_social_studio.sql`). **By day is the Plan's default** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "the date is the first row and the posts are below it and all in one row... slide...
select the date... a little bit bigger... I prefer that than the calendar"): `#days/<brand>/<up|past>/<filter>` lists each date with posts
(Coming up, the next 90 days; Past, the last 90, newest first), the date on top and its posts in one row that slides sideways
(`drawDays`, `.dayrow`, `.strip`); **Pick a date** or a date's heading opens that one date bigger (`#day/<brand>/<date>/<filter>`, Day
before / Day after, Every day back); **Calendar view** is the week grid below, kept as an option. The same page opens on **Plan**: a brand picker (`ve_social_brands`: house or
client, its Metricool brand and connected channels), the week Monday to Sunday (`#plan/<brand>/<monday>/<todo|out|posted|all>`, Back /
This week / Next week), one card a slot (`ve_social_slots`: time, channels, kind, title, caption, first comment, links, assets, By hand
steps, status), **Approve the N waiting**, and **New slot** for super admins. A slot (`#slot/<id>`): its pictures, Approve and schedule,
Skip it, **Change it directly** (every change a `ve_social_edits` row; a change to a scheduled slot is sent to Metricool again), and
**Notes** (`ve_social_notes`: Leave a note for Logan, optionally holding it as Changes asked; Logan marks each done with what he did;
**Notes for Logan** lists the open ones). Statuses: Waiting for approval, Changes asked, Approved, Scheduled, Posted, Did not post, Post
by hand, Skipped. **Approving pushes it**: `ve-social` creates the Metricool post (autoPublish, the slot's time in Eastern, Reel or
Story by kind); a brand not in Metricool, or a channel not connected for it, makes it **Post by hand** with the reason, known ahead of
time; skipping deletes it from Metricool. Cron `ve-social-sync` (every 15 minutes, `sync`, admin token) marks what went out Posted with
its links and copies its numbers from Metricool's analytics (matched by link) onto the slot, so a past week is the posted log with how
each did. Who: super admins edit every brand; anyone else by a `ve_social_people` row (editor or viewer), so a Community Manager or a
client can work their brand. Sean A. Russell and GeekFon Society are brands with no Metricool brand yet: add each in Metricool, then set
`metricool_blog_id` and `channels` on its row. Proven 2026-11-01 against the real Metricool: a [TEST] slot approved (scheduled), edited
(re-pushed, the old copy gone), skipped (removed), then deleted. **All three brands are in Metricool** (2026-11-01): Vegans Explore 3707345, GeekFon Society
7797245 (Instagram @geekfon, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok), Sean A. Russell 7797481 (Instagram @seanarussell82, Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube,
TikTok). A slot's assets are `{url, type}`: `image` and `video` go out; `cover` (the thumbnail on the Plan) and `storyboard` (frames for the
team) never do, and a reel, video or episode with no `video` asset cannot be pushed (it goes back to Changes asked, "No video yet"). Media
lives in `vegan-media/media/social/<batch>/` so Metricool can fetch it. **Relaunch week** (batch `relaunch-week`, from Station 2's lookbook,
loaded 2026-11-01): the Find your Guide carousel, the Airport and Dairy stories (link stickers by hand), the episode 144 clip, and one Guide
reel a day at 12:30 PM Eastern, Monday to Saturday (Thursday to Saturday are storyboards until their videos are made), each with Logan's
proposed caption and Station 2's `ve-relaunch` tracked links. **A slot shows its media as it will go out** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "I would like to see the actual asset in that
preview window... a light box and play for me... replace the item... you should get a notation of what change has been made"): the slot's
left panel is the preview in the post's shape (`mediaPanel`: stories, reels and episodes in a 9:16 frame, posts and carousels at their
own shape, a carousel with arrows and N of M), a warning when a wide picture would sit with bars on a story or reel, What goes out (each
file with **Replace** and **Remove**, and **Add a picture or video**), the cover (on the Plan only) and the storyboard (not posted). Any of
them opens full size in a **lightbox** (`lightbox`: videos play, arrows and the arrow keys move, Escape closes). A file goes up through
`ve-social` `asset_upload` (an editor of the brand; JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, MOV or WebM up to 300 MB; a signed upload into
`vegan-media/media/social/<brand>/<slot>/`), then the slot saves its assets (logged, and sent to Metricool again when it was scheduled).
**Plan cards show the whole picture** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "I would like to see the full item in the preview... It looks off to me"): every card's picture is a 4:5 frame; a reel, story, episode or video shows its cover whole on dark (`.th.v`, `contain`), and a post or carousel fills the frame from the top. **The period drives every tile** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "the tiles... don't appear to be synced with the dropdown... a custom option... how far back"): Last 7, 30, 90 days, 6 or 12 months, This year, each past year from 2023, or **Custom dates** (from and to, its own row; `range`, `periodSel`, `custRow` in `admin/depot/social.html`, kept for the visit in `sessionStorage` `ve_social`). Analytics opens with a summary strip for the period (views, posts, followers gained, likes, comments, the top post linked to its view), then one card per channel the brand has, led by its views in the period, its followers at the period's end and the change, posts, reach, likes, engagement and its top post. Metricool holds posts back to 2023 (Instagram and YouTube for Sean A. Russell) and follower counts from 2025; a card says when there is no follower history for the dates. **Notes can be spoken** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "Make it so I can leave a voice dictation on the post"): the note box has **Speak** (`wireSpeak` in `admin/depot/social.html`), the browser's own speech recognition writing at the cursor until Stop or silence, nothing recorded by us; no button where the browser has none (Firefox). The box is `data-dictate="off"` so `ve-dictate.js`'s floating mic does not double it. **A direct change by a person leaves Logan an open note** saying what changed (pictures and videos taken out and put in by file name, the
new time, Caption rewritten), in Notes for Logan; Logan's own changes leave none.
**Music** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "Instagram: Reels only, from Meta's library for outside apps. TikTok: the top 100 trending songs on photo and
carousel posts; videos with music get finished in the TikTok app"; migration `20261101_ve_social_sound_story.sql`). Checked against
Metricool's own OpenAPI spec (`app.metricool.com/api/swagger.json`, read through pg_net since the build session cannot reach it): Instagram
takes `instagramData.audioConfiguration` (`audioId` required, title, `audioType` music | original_sound, `audioVolume` and `videoVolume` 0 to
100) on Reels only, songs from `GET /v2/scheduler/catalogs/instagram/audio?searchQuery=`; TikTok takes `tiktokData.music` (`musicId`, title,
author, previewUrl, thumbnailUrl, and in practice `soundVolume`, refused without it though the spec does not mark it) on photo posts only,
songs from `GET /v2/scheduler/catalogs/tiktok/trending-tracks` (the top 100, `commercialMusicId`). A slot keeps its pick in
`ve_social_slots.sound` `{instagram?, tiktok?, by_hand?: {song}}`; the slot's **Music** panel (`musicPanel`, `wireMusic`) searches Instagram's
library (with Play to hear it and a mix: song and the video's own sound 100/100, song quieter under the voice 25/100, song only 100/0) on a
reel, video or episode, shows TikTok's top 100 (filter, Play, Pick) whenever TikTok is ticked, and takes **Not in the list?** (a song named
by hand). `ve-social` `sounds` {brand, net: instagram | tiktok, q?} reads the catalogs live. **What goes by hand, named ahead of time**: a
TikTok video with a song (TikTok is then Post by hand, "finish it in the TikTok app with <song>"), and a song named by hand (Instagram and
TikTok by hand unless a picked song covers them); the rest still schedules in Metricool. Instagram photo posts and stories get no song.
Proven 2026-11-01 against the real Metricool with [TEST] slots in December: a reel scheduled with its Instagram song at 25/100 and TikTok marked
by hand with the song named; a TikTok photo post scheduled with its song; then skipped (gone from Metricool) and the rows removed.
**Stories and Also share as a story** (same migration). A story slot goes to Metricool as type STORY; on 2026-11-01 a test story (today's
Find your Guide cover on a 9:16 frame) was scheduled on Vegans Explore's Instagram, Metricool held it as `instagramData.type` STORY, and it
published at 2:03 PM Eastern as an Instagram story (`instagram.com/stories/vegansexplore/...`). The same check found `sync` reading Metricool's
PUBLISHING as posted; only PUBLISHED or SUCCESS counts now.
A post's form has **Also share as a story** (any kind but story and thread): it adds a story slot 15 minutes after the post
(`STORY_AFTER_MIN`), on the post's Instagram and Facebook, with `story_of` the post, its links and a By hand link sticker step, and status
**held** (Waiting for 9:16 media) unless the post already has 9:16 media. Each picture and video carries its `w` and `h` (the page measures
them before saving, `measure`, `measureAll`); once every picture or video on a held story is 9:16 (height over width 1.70 to 1.86) it moves
to Waiting for approval, and back to held if a wide one goes on. A held story cannot be approved or pushed. The story follows the post's
time when the post moves, is skipped with it, and unticking the option skips it (out of Metricool if scheduled). `slot_get` returns the
post's `story` and the story's `parent`, linked on each slot. Proven 2026-11-01 with [TEST] slots (made held, moved to Waiting for approval
by a 1080 x 1920 picture, followed the post's move, skipped with it).
**Skipped slots are out of sight** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "When we skip a story, is it possible for us to delete or hide it? I don't like to see
things that we're not using"): the Plan (By day, a day, the Calendar view) and every chip leave skipped slots out, and a **Skipped** chip
shows only them (`inFilt` in `admin/depot/social.html`). A skipped slot has **Delete it** (an editor of the brand; `ve-social` `delete`,
refused with `not_skipped` for anything not skipped): the row goes, its notes and history with it (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), and a story made
from it keeps its own slot. Proven 2026-11-01 on a [TEST] slot (refused while waiting, skipped, deleted, its history gone).

to BrandDesk, it left the Go to menu, and the sender cron `ve-people-outreach` is unscheduled; 78 drafts stay in the table, unsent. The
table is kept for history (Depot > People reads its notes). The text below is history.

"Each day... see all the people I need to communicate with in all the different ways... when I click on it, it tells me exactly what
to do. It gives me the language. If it's an email... I approve it. It puts it on a schedule to go out... I have up until when it goes
out... If it's an Instagram message... me copying it... I just confirm that it was sent... text message... I respond in the notes with
what was said." **Depot > Outreach** (`/admin/depot/outreach`, People in the Go to menu; super admins), the Social studio's way of working
for one-to-one messages. Locked in V's outreach playbook: five buckets (business, community, sponsor, nonprofit, group), everyone Sean
knows reached by November 30, a weekend review. It lives in the Depot so it can be checked live from a build session; its tables are
shared, so it moves to HQ's People app unchanged.

- **A day** (`#day/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<todo|scheduled|finished|all>`): Day before / Today / Next day and a date picker, the days around it with
  how many still need Sean, a counter (need you, scheduled, done), and one row a person: initials, name and organization, the channel
  and bucket, what happened or why now, and the status (Needs you, Scheduled, Sent, Done, Skipped, Did not send). Anything left from
  earlier days shows as a banner on today (`#overdue`).
- **One message** (`#m/<id>`): what to do in one line, who and why now, where it goes (email, @handle with Open their Instagram via
  `ig.me/m/<handle>`, phone with Open Messages filled in, or the group), the tracked link in it with **Open the page** and its clicks, the
  words (editable). **Email**: Approve and schedule (goes out at its time, 10 AM Eastern on its day unless set; refused with no address,
  an empty subject or body, or a leftover `[Placeholder]`), Pull it back until then, Send me a test; changing the words of a scheduled one
  puts it back to Needs you. **Instagram, text, Meetup, call**: Copy, open the app, I sent it (or Done). Skip and Open it again. **Notes**
  are on the person (`person_key`: their email, `ig:<handle>`, or a key we set) and show on every message to them; **Follow up** puts them on
  a later day by any channel, a new draft. **Before and after** lists their other messages.
- **Data** (migration `20261101_people_outreach.sql`; RLS on, no policies): `ve_people_outreach` (one row a message: day, send_at,
  person, bucket, channel email | instagram | text | call | meetup | other, to_address, subject, body, link_code, why, personal,
  template_key, status draft | approved | sending | sent | done | skipped | failed), `ve_people_outreach_notes`, and
  `ve_people_outreach_templates` (the two or three base emails a bucket: approving one, `template_approve`, approves its messages that are
  not `personal`, and any later message made from it starts approved; personal ones always wait for Sean).
- **Server**: edge function `ve-people-outreach` (verify_jwt off; the VE token of a super admin, or `LESARUSS_ADMIN_TOKEN` with
  `as_member`): `day`, `overdue`, `get`, `save`, `approve`, `pull_back`, `done`, `skip`, `reopen`, `note`, `follow_up`, `test`, `create`,
  `templates`, `template_approve`, `tick`. Cron `ve-people-outreach` (every 5 minutes, x-cron-secret) runs `tick`: approved emails whose
  time has passed are claimed (`sending`), sent through `email-send` as brand `lesaruss` (from Sean A. Russell, replies to

## Money in: an email for every payment (Sean, 2026-11-01)

"John registered as a creator and made a payment, and I didn't get any notification that he made a payment... Is there something that
can be sent to me whenever we receive money?... branded and let me know what was purchased and by whom." Every live payment on the **Vegans
Explore** Stripe account that the webhook (`ve-stripe-webhook`) receives sends one email to
contact@lesaruss.com (since 2026-11-05, Sean: "I just want to see transactions from Vegans Explore": payments on the Meatless Muscle
and LESARUSS accounts send none, nor does a customer tagged `revenue_class: client_services`, Brooke's billing; `moneyAlert`) from VEGANS EXPLORE <hello@vegansexplore.com>, before any product's own branch runs, so a new product is covered with
no change: a paid Checkout session (`checkout.session.completed` or `async_payment_succeeded`, amount over $0) and a subscription renewal
(`invoice.payment_succeeded` other than `subscription_create`, which is its Checkout session). Subject "$11.00 in: <product> from <name>";
the email (`moneyEmail`): the brand's header (Vegans Explore's mark, else the brand's name), Money in or Renewal paid, the amount, the
product (`MONEY_LABELS` by `metadata.type`, else the line item), their first payment when it is, What (Stripe's line items), Who (name and
@username), Email, Member (Founding Member or Member, role, home chapter, account since), When (Eastern), Paid to (which Stripe account),
**See it in Stripe**, and This month so far (Eastern month). `ve_money_alerts` (migration `20261101_ve_money_alerts.sql`, RLS on, no
policies) keeps one row per payment (`stripe_id` unique), so a Stripe retry never sends twice; `sent_at` or `send_error`. Test mode sends
nothing. A new product reads best with a `MONEY_LABELS` row. **Preview** any real session: POST
`ve-stripe-webhook?money_preview=<cs_...>` with `Authorization: Bearer <LESARUSS_ADMIN_TOKEN>` ([Preview] subject, no row). **Labels by what it is** (2026-11-01, v63 from commit 46ab777, source sha256 matched): `moneyLabel` names the one type that covers several
products from the session itself: `ve_verified` is the Partner plan ($111 every 111 days, with its offer and period) or Passport Stop or Anchor by
`metadata.tier` (it was "VE Verified (yearly)" for all of them); `entry_contribution` is a listing claim when it carries `claim_id`, a contribution
when the buyer was a member over an hour before, else the Passport. HQ's LESARUSS-account kinds have labels (`lr_passport`, `listing_claim`,
`guide_order`, `business_membership`, `campaign_pledge`), and a renewal is labeled from its subscription's metadata
(`parent.subscription_details`, else `subscription_details`) instead of the raw invoice line. **This month** counts from midnight Eastern on the
1st, read from the zone (04:00Z under EDT, 05:00Z under EST; it was always 04:00Z, which would have put Nov 30 11 PM in December). Untyped
sessions (payment links such as the LIVE Donation) read well from their own line item and need no label. Payments before
2026-11-01 2:36 PM Eastern sent nothing; John Thomas's $11 Passport (11:00 AM that day) was sent as the first preview. Deployed as version 62
from commit 3292d5a (source sha256 matched; the deployed source was checked against main first).

## Three doors, one Welcome, campaigns on people (LOCKED by Sean 2026-11-03, playbooks `ve-pathways`, `ve-pricing-points-passport`)

Concept session with V, locked by Sean: "we can lock it" (canon `canon-ve-people-campaigns-doors`; migration
`20261103_people_campaigns_doors_canon.sql`; the full write-up, build order and open question are
`docs/proposals/people-campaigns-doors.md`: read it before building any of this). **Built so far (below): the member card, the survey door, Pulse subscribe (dark) and the people sender. Not built: the updated Welcome, profiles with groups, campaign homes.**
Sean: "people don't have to pay to get in, but they do have to show some effort."

- **Three doors, no comps**: a free **Daily Pulse subscription** (an email; cities picked; not a membership); the **survey**
  (membership, full access, 250 points); the **$11** (membership, full access, 1,100 points). Bonus points are given by hand from a
  member's card. **Founding Member (Sean, 2026-11-03: "Yes, anyone who becomes a member before January is a founding member.")**: either door, before midnight Eastern on 2027-01-01, makes a Founding Member (the survey door too, not only the $11).
- **One Welcome**: the Welcome, the Passport and the Taste merge into one free, public guide that explains how to use Vegans
  Explore and ends with the two paths. The Taster account type goes away; `ve-taster`, `/guides/taste` and the Taster emails keep
  working until then, and Pulse subscribers get no Taster sequence.

  days, double opt-in, daily or weekly per city, a short issue with a From Vegans Explore slot for campaigns.

  (Noticed, Interested, Committed); default follow-up Day 0, 3, 7, 14; a two-week calendar approved once; a campaign lives in
  BrandDesk (its Plan tab becomes **Playbook**) with Overview, People, Assets, Messages, Playbook, Results.
- **The people sender** (BCPS Marcom's way, rebuilt on Depot > Outreach): pick people and make drafts, Sent / Opened / Clicked on
  every row and a campaign table, then a week view. Nothing sends until Sean approves each message.
- **Built 2026-11-03**: the dashboard's member card opens from a Recent Members, Votes, Leads, Leaderboard or Inbox picture or name
  (Recent Members lists only Vegans Explore members, `identity_source` `members`), and **Take back** points sits beside Give
  (`ve_points_take`, `ve-dashboard` `take_points`: spendable only, never lifetime, never below zero, a reason required, once per
  ref). The button was proven in the database, not yet clicked in a browser. Hover rings are no longer clipped in the dashboard's
  scrolling boxes.
- **The survey door, built 2026-11-03** (Sean: "move forward"; migration `20261103_survey_door.sql`, applied through the one-time `ve-once-survey-door`,
  now the 410 stub). An account waiting on its Passport (`pending_payment`) opens `/survey?door=1` (the join window's **Take the survey instead - free**),
  `ve-mission-survey` `door_start` (`ve_survey_door_start`) sets `members.survey_door_at`, and `ve_profile_answer` then accepts its answers (it refused anyone
  not active before). Each answer pays its points as always (250 in all, the survey's own, never the 1,100); the last one admits the account
  (`ve_survey_door_admit`: `membership_status` active, `entry_via` `survey`, `entry_paid_at` stays null, since nothing was paid). **Founding**:
  `ve_founding_on_paid` now also fires when a survey door account turns active before `ve_founding_deadline()`; the brand membership is its own kind,
  `survey` (not a comp). `ve_referral_on_admit` already pays the sharer 111 points for a join with no payment (Level 2 gets the commission only on a payment).
  `members.entry_via` is `passport` for everyone who paid (backfilled) and `survey` here; older comps are null. Proven 2026-11-03 in a rolled-back transaction
  (refused before the door, 250 of 250 admits, active, `survey`, no `entry_paid_at`, Founding, brand membership `survey`). Wording: the join window, the Passport's
  Get your Passport tab, `/policies#membership`, `ve-guide-platform-facts` (`knowledge_records` `body.facts`, its old 30% top rate and "everyone joins with the $11"
  fixed) and six saved answers. **Not yet**: the page checked in a browser as an unpaid account, `/claim` and the pages with their own join step (`VE_ACTIVATE_HANDLER`)
  do not offer the survey, nothing stops one person making many unpaid accounts to farm the 111-point referral (Sean's call), and the three challenges are not retired.

## The Explorer path and badges (LOCKED by Sean 2026-11-06, playbook `ve-outreach`)

"Lock it" (canon `canon-ve-door-guides` v7, key `explorer_path_v7`; voice canon `canon-ve-voice-hero-guide`; migration
`20261106_explorer_path_v7_canon.sql`). **Not built yet; queued behind Checking in's Monday sends and the Hot Lab meetings merge.** Sean: "if
I was on that list, what would you give me? I'm a business owner, I do events, I have groups, I'm a content creator... you're going to guess."
So we stop picking a door per person: everyone takes Explorer, then chooses their own paths. It replaces the parts of v6 and of "Three doors"
above that it contradicts (the person check at the door, the 31 questions as the door).

- **Explorer is everyone's door and path** (part 1): the Welcome tour (about 3 minutes) plus the 8-question `explorer` survey (about 2
  minutes). Finishing it makes them a member at once, with the **Explorer badge**; no person check, the abuse watch is the guard. The 31
  questions become **Build your profile**, filled in over time and paid per answer.
- **The paths page** comes next: every path as a card to preview and start (Creator, Restaurant, Event host, Nonprofit, Business, later Group
  leader), ordered by "Do you run any of these?", never hidden. People take as many as fit.
- **Path Guides are part 2**, about the path only. Locked in the catalog until Explorer ("Starts after Explorer"); reached early, Explorer opens
  inside the Guide as its first step; with the badge that step shows done and they go straight to the path's intake. Topic Guides ($11 or 1,100
  points) are not gated. Existing members take Explorer too.
- **Points**: every survey is 250 for answering everything; required questions are few and worth less, optional and open ones more, weighted
  by how useful the answer is. Explorer: chapter 15, journey 15, Do you run any of these 20 (required); what brings you 30, what you want more
  of 35, how to hear from us 15, a place or person to add 45, in your own words 75. Add "I organize a group or community" and "Another kind of
  business" to Do you run any of these.
- **Badges**: Explorer, then Registered creator, restaurant owner, event host, nonprofit, business (automatic on finishing the intake), Group
  leader later; Ambassador invitation only; each badge a `ve_person_tags` tag. A badge opens its Guide and its opportunities, never money.
- **One invitation for everyone**, plus a restaurant version on the business's personal link (Explorer first, then their Restaurant path).
  **Voice: they are the hero, we are the guide** (Sean: "It's about them"): open on what they do for the community, say what opens for them;
  never open on our launch or ask them to support us or join our journey. Every email is a draft for Sean.

  straight-in admission; 4 the paths page; 5 path Guides gated with Explorer inline; 6 badges on profiles and as tags; 7 Build your profile;

## Abuse watch: a judge decides (Sean, 2026-11-03)

"Have some sort of security mechanism that looks for abuse... if an account is suspected of trying to game the system, internally we can
start tracking them... if it turns out they have abused the system, any points they have will be null and void, and they will be either
suspended or banned." Sean is the judge: every suspend, ban and void is his decision, never the system's. Migration
`20261103_abuse_watch.sql` (applied through the one-time `ve-once-abuse-watch`, now the 410 stub).

- **Tables** (RLS on, no policies): `ve_abuse_cases` (one open case a member: watching, cleared, voided, suspended, banned), `ve_abuse_signals`
  (one row a member, kind and day, with its evidence) and `ve_abuse_events` (every move, who and why). `members.standing` is good, suspended
  or banned.
- **The scan** `ve_abuse_scan()` (cron `ve-abuse-scan`, 9:11 UTC daily) records signals: `referral_burst` (5 sign-ups on one link in 24 hours, 30),
  `fast_survey` (survey door finished in under 2 minutes, 40), `disposable_email` (20), `points_velocity` (over 3,000 earned in 24 hours, 25),
  `checkin_pace` (4 places in an hour, 25), `survey_only_referrals` (3 or more survey joins and no paid one, 15). A score is each kind once over
  14 days. Only `member_class` member, never super admins. **Log-only until Sean turns it on** (`ve_site_settings` `abuse_watch`: `mode`
  `log_only` | `on`, `open_at` 40, `watch_days` 30, `log_only_until` 2026-11-10): in log-only it opens no case and the scan returns who would
  have opened. Logan's defaults, Sean's to change.
- **The judge's functions** (service role only, a super admin and a note required, all logged): `ve_abuse_watch` (open a case by hand),
  `ve_abuse_decide` with `clear`, `void`, `restore_points`, `suspend`, `ban` and `reinstate`. **Suspend freezes points and participation and is
  reversible; a ban is permanent but can be undone with `reinstate`.** A void sets the balance and lifetime points to zero, writes an
  `abuse_void` ledger row and keeps what it took in `void_snapshot`, so `restore_points` puts it back (`abuse_restore`). Nothing is deleted.
- **The freeze** is `trg_ve_members_freeze_guard`: a suspended or banned account's `lesars_balance` cannot change, so every function that earns
  or spends points raises `account_frozen` (proven in a rolled-back transaction; void and restore pass a transaction-local bypass). Risk to
  check before the first suspension: a cron that loops over members (`ve_vault_settle`, `ve_challenge_settle`) would stop at a frozen one.
- **Devices** (migration `20261103_abuse_watch_devices.sql`, `ve-auth` version 71 from c7ddf70, source sha256 matched): every email and Google
  sign-up writes a `ve_member_devices` row (`recordMemberDevice`: the IP's salted hash, the same one `ve_signup_attempts` keeps, and a salted
  hash of the browser id the page keeps in `localStorage` `ve_visitor`, sent by `public/ve-auth.js` as `visitor`; best effort, never blocks a
  sign-up; RLS on, no policies). Five existing sign-ups were backfilled with their IP hash. `ve_abuse_scan_devices()` (cron
  `ve-abuse-scan-devices`, 9:09 UTC, before the scan) adds `shared_browser` (three or more accounts on one browser in 30 days, 35) and `shared_ip`
  (four or more on one network in 7 days, 20: offices, homes and events share one, so it is weak alone). Browser ids reach the server only once
  the page's `ve-auth.js` is on `main`; until then only the IP signal fills. Proven in a rolled-back transaction.
- **Standing is enforced at sign-in** (`ve-auth` and `ve-votes` from e2c549c, source sha256 matched): `standingBlock` in `ve-auth` refuses email
  login (after the password is right), Google sign-in, `me` (so a session in a browser drops) and `requireActiveMembership`; `ve-votes` refuses a
  vote. A suspended account reads "suspended while our team reviews it, your points are on hold"; a banned one "this account has been closed";
  neither says why, both give contact@lesaruss.com (403, `code` `account_suspended` or `account_banned`). Checked: the normal paths still
  answer live. The 15 token-only functions that take part now refuse writes the same way (below); the rest check only the token, so an old
  session could still do something there until it expires, while points are frozen everywhere regardless.
- **Depot > Watchlist** (`/admin/depot/watchlist`, People in the Go to menu, built 2026-11-03 on the Feedback page's shell; edge function `ve-abuse`
  from 7a4085a, source sha256 matched, verify_jwt off, super admin token checked inside, the signed-in admin is the judge): tabs Watching, **Would
  flag** (log-only: who the scan would have opened a case for), Suspended, Banned, Points voided, Cleared, All cases, and **Watch someone**
  (`#new`: find a member by name or email). A banner says whether opening cases is on (**Turn on opening cases** / Back to log only, `set_mode`).
  One case per view (`#case/<id>`, `#member/<id>` before a case exists): who they are and how they joined, **Why they were flagged** (every
  signal with what we saw), **Points** (balance, lifetime, the ledger), **People around them** (who they joined through, who they brought in with
  how each joined, other accounts on the same browser or network; a busy network is counted, not named), the history, and **Your decision**: a
  required note, then Clear, Void their points, Restore their points, Suspend, Ban or Reinstate as the case allows, each behind a confirm
  that says what it does. `ve-abuse` actions `list`, `get`, `find`, `watch`, `decide`, `set_mode`; you cannot open a case on or decide your own
  account. Proven live 2026-11-03 as Sean through a one-time function on the Test Manager account (no token 401, a non-admin 403, list, find,
  get, watch with no note and on yourself refused, watch, a second watch refused, void, a second void refused, restore, suspend, reinstate, ban,
  unban, the history, a bad decision and a bad mode refused; then every row removed). The page checked at 1440 and 390 px beside Feedback.
- **Freeze safety, built and live 2026-11-03** (migration `20261103_abuse_freeze_safety.sql`, applied through the one-time `ve-once-freeze-safety`, now the 410 stub): `ve_member_frozen(member)`; `ve_points_grant` returns `{granted:false, frozen:true}` for a frozen member instead of raising; `ve_vault_settle` only lets members in good standing win and settles each card in its own block (a freeze that lands mid-run extends the card); `ve_challenge_settle` returns `{status:'held'}` for a frozen member (not paid, not expired) and `ve_challenge_sweep` handles each challenge on its own; `ve_hunt_award` returns false; `ve_bounty_pay` and `ve_recipe_review` (approve) return `account_frozen` before changing anything; `universe_join_from_purchase` still takes the order but pays 0 points to a frozen buyer. Proven 2026-11-03 in a rolled-back transaction on Test Manager (a suspended bidder and a suspended challenger: vault extended not raised, grant frozen, challenge held and not expired, balance untouched; a good bidder still won). **Direct-balance writers left as they were** because a person starts them and the edge-function check below stops a frozen member first: `award_points_bounty`, `back_campaign_with_points`, `credit_points_purchase` (credits are retired), `donate_points_to_nonprofit`, the `spend_points_for_*` functions, `ve_checkin_save`, `ve_credit_from_points`, `ve_listing_contribute`, `ve_listing_submit_points`. If one of them gains a caller that is a cron or a webhook, give it the same `ve_member_frozen` guard.

Proven live 2026-11-03 with a session for Test Manager suspended for a few seconds: a write on each of the 15 answered 403 and reads on `ve-board`, `ve-vault`, `ve-checkin`, `ve-cookbook` and `ve-mission-survey` answered 200 (`ve-once-standing-proof`, now the 410 stub; standing put back to good). Other edge functions (`ve-dashboard`, `ve-affiliate`, `ve-bounties` aside, `ve-people-outreach`, `ve-nonprofit`, `ve-ambassador`...) still check only the token; points are frozen everywhere by the trigger regardless.

## The survey is the only way in (LOCKED by Sean 2026-11-07, playbook `ve-pricing-points-passport`, canon `canon-ve-door-guides` v12)

"We don't want to inhibit them from being able to complete the survey, and we really don't even want them to bypass the survey...
Stopping them at the door for $11." Replaces "Registration is the Passport", "Guide pricing, points and levels" and the two-door parts of
"Three doors" where they conflict. **Built and live 2026-11-07**:
- **Membership is free; the survey is the only way in** (the Explorer survey, or a business Guide's survey), 250 points, no welcome points.
  The $11 window in `public/ve-auth.js` leads with Take the survey; its $11 button shows only for another brand's account the server sent to
  checkout (`_needUrl`). The sign-up tab reads **Join free**, its button Continue to the survey. `/passport` Enter the room is one card (the
  survey, `/survey?s=explorer`); `/business` Get started is Join free, then claim free. `ve-votes.js` members-only prompts say join free.
- **The Vegan Dairy Guide is LOCKED as the prototype** (Sean, 2026-11-07: "beautiful... the prototype... it has value right now for $11"): Maya opens and explains it, the animation makes the difference; other Guides keep still images for now, animation later. Change it only on Sean's word. The front pages of the topic Guides no longer state the price (the $11 box in the header already says it): no "The full Guide is $11 or 1,100 points" line, and the venue Guides' button reads Get the Guide.
- **Topic Guides' buy box** (Sean, 2026-11-07: "just like an airline... pick either or. Anything else other than that is complicating it"): the public sees **$11** and **Member? Sign in**; a signed-in member sees **$11 or 1,100 points** and picks (Use 1,100 points / Pay $11; short of points, $11 with their balance and a bounties link). No copy says buying a Guide makes you a member, in the six topic Guide scripts (Dairy, Nutrition, Airport, Stadium & Arena, Theme Park, Supermarket). The server still admits a Guide buyer (`ve_guide_purchase_paid`) on purpose: an account that is not a member is treated as signed out on every page, so without it someone who paid could not open what they bought.

  `claim.html` offers Claim it free / Add it free first and the Partner plan second; a non-member goes to the survey and back, `_add_` for Add it).

  migration `20261107_survey_only_door.sql`). Referral points (111) continue. Earned commissions are still paid.

Concept session with V, locked by Sean: "lock it" (canon `canon-ve-holiday-guide`; migration `20261107_holiday_guide_canon.sql`; handoff

hand first: business holiday menus by chapter, a gift list we compile (credited, never copied; tracked `/go/` links), member wish lists feeding

- **Free and public**; join prompts only at moments of intent (Save, Add to my wish list, Remind me, Submit your holiday menu), one short
  window, what they tapped kept through sign-up and saved once they are in. People join by the Explorer survey (one optional question: What
  are you hoping to find this season?); businesses: join free, the Restaurant or Pre-Vegan Business survey, claim free, then the menu form with
  the deadline counting down. An exception to topic Guides being $11.
- **ThanksLiving** is the first holiday: the fourth Thursday of November (2026-11-26), shown as ThanksLiving (Thanksgiving) the first year so
  search finds it. The word is shared (sanctuary fundraisers, Explore Veg, vKind, Christian writing; no trademark found, Justia only): never
  claim we coined it or try to trademark it; we become where everyone finds it, every sanctuary's ThanksLiving event on our calendar. Five
  rules: three thanks (a person, a place, a thing on your table), the Gratitude Table (a shared plant-based meal), say it out loud, give back,
  start your reflection. Never tear down Thanksgiving; the same day is the National Day of Mourning, so point to Indigenous-led voices.
  "Gratitude Day" was dropped (World Gratitude Day is September 21).
- **Business menus**: any member business with a claimed listing, free, person-checked, 100% Vegan first, a business that is not Vegan shows a
  plant-based (Pre-Vegan) menu; any holiday is the same form. A dated `ve_dashboard_cards` card and a holiday hours field on Your page. A
  one-time note to restaurants with a published email is drafted for Sean; nothing sends without him.

  we never handle money or call anything tax-deductible. Nonprofit Partners featured, every other Directory nonprofit, rescue and sanctuary

"Instead of sending people to their page, let's send them to the directory listing, and then on the directory listings, have the donation link

cards open `/directory/<slug>` (places with a donation link first). A Nonprofits, Rescues or Sanctuaries listing shows **Donate** at the top of its
Overview (`giveCta` in `directory/listing.html`) and **Why support <name>** under About (`giveWhy`), both from `listings.details`: `support`
{text, words, sources, written_at, model, note}, `donation_url` (`donation_url_source` `ve-giveback` when we found it; one the team or the owner
set is never replaced) and `donation_link_code`, the organization's own tracked link (`ve_links` code `give-<slug>`, initiative `give-back`), so
`ve-links` counts and names every click. Written by edge function **`ve-giveback`** (verify_jwt off; super admin, admin token or cron secret;
`one` {slug, save?}, `batch` {slugs (25), wait?}): it reads their home, about and donate pages, collects giving links from their own site or known
giving platforms, and Claude (Opus 5.5, 16000, end_turn only) writes 400 to 550 words when the site has that much and less when it does not, from
their site only, never a tax claim, never calling them Vegan unless they say so; the donation link is picked only from the links found. A failed
try leaves `details.support_try` {at, why}. We never handle money. Pilot 2026-11-08: 20 Florida organizations, 19 written (218 to 466 words), 17
with a donation link (Piper's Pals and Nathans Family Farm show none on their sites), Little Bear Sanctuary's site did not open from the server.

the same day** ("I love it... ## What connects to a listing: our episodes, other shows, people (Sean, 2026-11-08, playbook `ve-community-directory`)

"The directory listing is designed for discovery. So anytime we can have something that's related or connected, it needs to be there."
`ve_listing_related(listing)` (public RPC) reads `ve_listing_related_cache`, built by `ve_listing_related_build` and refreshed by cron
`ve-listing-related` (every 2 hours at :17, 25 listings, each rebuilt after a day; migration `20261108_listing_related.sql`): **ours** (our four
shows' episodes that name the listing, from `ve_content_mentions`, matched to the feed through `ve_pulse_episode_map` so they play), **elsewhere**
(other Directory podcasts' episodes whose title or show notes name it, 40 at most, `how` featured when the title names it or one of its people,
else mentioned; organizations and groups only), **people** (People listings whose title or bio names it, those whose title names it first) and,
on a person, **orgs** (the reverse). Names (`ve_listing_related_names`): the name without "The" or a parenthesis, the same without a trailing
Sanctuary / Rescue / Inc / Foundation / Society, and `details.aka`; two words and 9 letters or more, or a name that is wholly capitals (PETA); a
name of only generic words ("animal advocates") counts only as a full name of three words or more or one that goes by "The"; any other listing's
longer name that contains it is blanked first, so Farm Sanctuary does not match Woodstock Farm Sanctuary. A wrong match is fixed by `details.aka`
or the listing's name. **The page** (`loadRelated` in `directory/listing.html`): People (or Organizations on a person) as Directory cards, then On our
podcast and On other podcasts as episode rows with Play in a docked player, right after About; then **In the Pulse**, which had no caller on real
listings until now, draws the articles that are not episodes shown above. Films and books keep their own episode sections. First built 2026-11-08:
834 listings, 74 with our episodes (playable), 70 with other shows (582 episodes), 14 organizations with people and 14 people with their organizations.

## Social links and price on listings (Sean, 2026-11-08, playbook `ve-feedback`)

"$2" on listings and "Facebook opens the plain Facebook page, Instagram a broken page". Fixed and live on `main` (ec8f871).
- **Price**: `listings.google_price_level` held Google's raw level (1 to 4) from an old import. It is stored and shown as `$` to `$$$$`
  (migration `20261108_price_level_dollars.sql`: `ve_price_level_dollars()`, trigger `trg_ve_listings_price_level` turns any raw number or
  `PRICE_LEVEL_*` name written later into dollar signs; 48 rows changed, each a `ve_listing_edits` row). Hand-entered ranges ("$10–20") stay.
  The listing page maps 1 to 4 too. No function writes the column today.
- **One link builder**: `socialUrl(net, value)` in `directory/listing.html` builds every social link (the sidebar Follow buttons, the
  "Find them on" icons, schema.org `sameAs`). It takes a full link, `@handle`, `handle` or `site.com/handle`, drops trailing text and a link
  to the wrong network. Before, a bare Facebook handle became a link relative to our own site. `esc()` now escapes quotes.
- **The stored values were the real problem.** Scan of every approved listing (tables `ve_social_link_checks`, `ve_social_scan_ig`, run
  `social-2026-11-08`): Instagram through Apify's profile scraper (885 handles, $2.04, misses run twice): 34 accounts that no longer exist
  (Honest Cuban's `@vegancubancuisine` among them; `@honestcuban` exists with 9 posts but is not confirmed theirs), 15 `@rsrc.php` and one
  `@accounts`, all cleared; `fish_defender,` fixed. Facebook: 25 system pages (16 `facebook.com/docs`, 5 `/login`, `/help`, `/2008`, `/external-redirect`...)
  cleared (27 listings), Blue Moon Cafe's trailing text trimmed. Every removed value is kept in `listings.details.social_removed` and logged in
  `ve_listing_edits` (`meta.playbook` ve-feedback). Migration note `20261108_social_links_cleanup.sql`.
- **Where the junk came from**: the home-page readers (`ve-restaurant-audit` essentials, `ve-discover`, `ve-logo-hunt`) matched
  `instagram.com/` anywhere in a link, so `static.cdninstagram.com/rsrc.php/...` read as `@rsrc.php`, and took Facebook's own pages from site
  footers. Both now require `instagram.com` as the host and skip Facebook's and Instagram's system paths (`TEMPLATE_HANDLES`). Deployed from
  2abef85 (ve-restaurant-audit v22, ve-discover, ve-logo-hunt v11; source sha256 matched). ve-discover's live copy had been behind main
  (no Google meter, max_tokens 4000, no Event Venues or Promoters); v23 brought it level.
- **Checking a Facebook page from the server is not reliable**: logged out, Facebook answers a search-crawler request for a real page with
  its title and a missing one with the login wall, but after about 60 requests it sends everything to login. Apify's pages scraper says
  "not available" for real people whose profiles hide from logged-out visitors (Tabitha Brown, Isa Chandra). Never remove a Facebook link on
  "not available" alone; list it for a person to look at. Instagram's own API returns 404 or 429 to our server, so Instagram checks go
  through Apify.

## Image conventions

- Mobile hero images: stored in the same folder as the page's desktop banner.
  Named `ve-[page]-mobile.png`.
- Desktop hero images: referenced in the page's `.hero` CSS via `background-image`.

## Hero legibility pattern (LOCKED 2026-05-18)

Desktop (Option A): strong left-to-right gradient overlay.
```css
.hero::before {
  background: linear-gradient(to right,
    rgba(0,0,0,0.99) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0.95) 28%,
    rgba(0,0,0,0.72) 52%, rgba(0,0,0,0.28) 68%,
    transparent 84%);
}
.hero::after {
  background: linear-gradient(to top, rgba(0,0,0,0.45) 0%, transparent 32%);
}
```

Mobile (Option B): flat scrim + frosted glass card.
```css
@media (max-width: [breakpoint]px) {
  .hero { background-image: url('/path/to/ve-[page]-mobile.png'); background-position: center center; align-items: flex-end; }
  .hero::before { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.32); }
  .hero::after { display: none; }
  .hero-inner { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.58); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px); border-radius: 8px; margin: 0 24px 32px; padding: 32px 28px; max-width: calc(100% - 48px); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.09); }
}
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .hero::before { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.32); }
  .hero::after { display: none; }
  .hero-inner { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.62); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px); border-radius: 8px; margin: 0 16px 24px; padding: 28px 24px; max-width: calc(100% - 32px); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.10); }
}
```

## Database writes the connector holds (Sean, 2026-10-25)

"We've been through this before, and you did something that allowed it to work... build into our instructions so we do
it moving forward." Canon `ops-supabase-write-once-function`, error registry `SUPABASE-MCP-APPROVAL-HOLD-USE-ONCE-FUNCTION`.
When the Supabase connector's `execute_sql` or `apply_migration` holds a write for an approval box that never shows (it
times out at 60 s, "the server asked the user a question"), do not retry it and do not hand Sean SQL to paste. Run it through
a one-time edge function instead: copy `scripts/supabase-once/once.template.ts`, put the SQL in named steps (each one safe to
run twice), give it a fresh random key kept only in the session scratchpad, deploy it as `ve-once-<task>` with verify_jwt
off, run each step with `curl -X POST .../functions/v1/ve-once-<task>?step=<name> -H "x-run-key: <key>"`, check the result
with a plain SELECT (reads and deploys never prompt), then redeploy it as the 410 stub. The SQL still goes in a migration
file in the repo. A step runs in one transaction, so a failed step changes nothing.

## Google costs: a $50 monthly hard stop and standing approval (Sean, 2026-11-04, playbook `ve-spend-budget`)

"I wasn't fully aware of all of this." **The rule now** (Sean, 2026-11-04: "I'm willing to put a $50 budget for Google on that... that's the cap... All I ask for is a report of the
activity, what's been spent, at the end of each week"; canon `canon-ve-spend-budget`). **Google is a hard $50 a month**, counted at list price with no
free tier (the free amounts are unverified; Google's own bill, Cloud Billing > Reports, filter Places API, is the truth). Sean raises the cap when things
move faster (`ve_site_settings` `google_budget` `monthly_cap_usd`). **Standing approval**: Logan runs any Google scan whose quote fits what is left under
the cap, without asking, and reports it weekly; a scan that would cross the cap stops and asks. This replaces the 2026-11-01 rule to ask before any scan of
about 200 calls. **A quote is a ceiling**: a one-time scan is approved with `ve_google_approve('once:<task>', searches, details, note)`, which refuses
(`over_cap`, with what is left) when its list cost is more than the ledger's left, and the scan checks `ve_google_once_room('once:<task>', 'search'|'details')`
before every batch and stops at 0; close it with `ve_google_close`. A batch is counted after it is sent, so a scan can pass its ceiling by at most the one
batch in flight. **The ledger** is `ve_google_ledger()` (cap, spent, regular, approved-not-yet-run, left, every approval; also `ledger` in
`ve_google_report`). **Enforced in the room check** every caller already makes: `ve_google_room` is the smaller of the day's cap and the month's, background
jobs stop at 60% of the month's cap (`background_month_share`) so a person's action and an approved scan keep room, and at the cap everything reads 0.
**Daily caps raised to 120 searches and 100 details** (background 60% of it); an approved one-time scan runs outside the daily cap, as before. Google's own
limit is 500 text searches a day across the project. Migration `20261104_google_hard_cap_ledger.sql`. Proven 2026-11-04 in a rolled-back transaction (no
approval no room; over-cap, bad-name and duplicate approvals refused; room and committed fell with usage; past the cap every room read 0). Month to date
2026-11-04: $14.00 at list, $36.01 left. Not yet: the weekly snapshot and Sunday email, the BrandDesk Costs module, Apify and Higgsfield usage in the ledger
(`ve-spend-budget` steps 2 to 4). The earlier rule's text follows for history.

Google Places bills the Google Cloud account's card monthly past its free monthly amount (Text
Search about $32 per 1,000 past about 5,000 a month; Place Details and PageSpeed have their own). The project's cap is 500 text searches a
day, shared by every job (the backlog check every 2 minutes, the nightly essentials pass, the audits, Add a listing, imports). **Before any
scan of more than about 200 Google calls, give Sean the call count and the estimated cost, and wait for his go.** Schedule big imports right
after the midnight-Pacific reset and split them across nights rather than raising the cap. Sean sees the bill in Google Cloud > Billing >
Reports (filter Places API); a budget alert lives in Billing > Budgets & alerts.
**The meter and caps** (Sean, 2026-11-01: "we need to be monitoring this carefully and setting caps"; migration
`20261101_google_spend_meter.sql`): every Places request from `ve-discover`, `ve-listing-about`, `ve-restaurant-audit` and `ve-venues` is
counted in `ve_google_usage` (day, search | details, job; `ve_google_count`), and each job checks `ve_google_room` before it starts: a
background job (backlog check, essentials, About writer, check-ups) runs only a batch that fits its share of the day's cap and otherwise waits
for tomorrow (so nothing is marked not found for lack of an answer), and what a person starts (Add a listing, the free and full audit, Find on
Google) gets `google_limit` only when the whole cap is used. Caps, the background share, list prices, free monthly amounts and the monthly
budget are `ve_site_settings` `google_budget` (Logan's defaults: 40 searches and 40 place details a day, background 60%, $15 a month).
**Depot > Analytics > Google costs** (`#google`, `ve-analytics` returns `ve_google_report`) shows today against the caps, the month's
requests and estimated cost against the budget, and every day by job. A one-time scan Sean approves runs outside the daily cap but counts
toward the month (`once:<task>`). Other Google services we use (YouTube, Books, Analytics, sign-in, PageSpeed) are free and not metered.

## pg_net stalls (2026-10-28)

Every cron that calls an edge function, and `ve-function-deploy` called from SQL, goes through pg_net's one worker. On 2026-10-28
it sat on one batch for 12 minutes (`net.http_request_queue` growing, `max(id)` in `net._http_response` not moving, the worker's
`state_change` in `pg_stat_activity` old). `net.worker_restart()` did not free it; `pg_terminate_backend` on the `pg_net%` worker
did, a minute later a new worker drained the queue (requests waiting in the queue are kept). Check that first when a cron's work
stops landing.

## People campaigns in BrandDesk, and founding cohort 1 (Sean, 2026-11-08, playbook `ve-outreach-buckets`)

"It was always our intention to send to people who aren't business owners... built into the outreach, and so we can track it the way we track
everything else." A BrandDesk campaign with `audience` `people` holds members by email (`ve_outreach_campaign_members.person_key`, plus
`person_name`, `person_id`), no listing, and sends through the same `campaignTick` with the same rules and the same per-member tracked `/go/` link
and `email_sends` rows (migration `20261108_people_campaigns.sql`; `ve-outreach` from 3ec1db0, sha256 bb430bd9; it still has `campaignTick`). Each
person's outreach contact is segment `person` on the list `people-campaigns`, which is never switched on. A campaign's `footer_reason` words the
footer. HQ (branch `claude/focused-fermi-o89hgt`, not on HQ main): a People tile, person rows, preview and test by `member_id`, and Opened / Clicked
on every campaign row. **Cohort 1** `founding-cohort-1-2026-11`: 151 from Suggested for Vegans Explore (list `docs/proposals/founding-cohort-1-list.md`),
from Sean, to the Welcome Guide, start Mon Nov 9, a draft until Sean locks and approves; three Wednesday Holiday Guide follow-ups by engagement
(`founding-cohort-1-wed-clicked|opened|quiet`), drafts with no people until Wednesday morning. Handoff
